info.title: Yagra northbound API
info.description:
The REST surface of Yagra-core: inventory, metrics, alerts, passive events and configuration.

This document is generated from the Rust handlers — it is the contract, not a description of one.

200.description: Every active alert, each decorated with its inbound ack state
The ack was recorded (or cleared) and broadcast

400.description: Neither `node` nor a readable `subject` was supplied

404.description: The subject is outside the caller's group scope

503.description: This deployment has no ack store

get.summary: Alert fires bucketed weekday×hour over the last `days` (for the calendar heatmap).

200.description: Weekday×hour fire counts; empty when this deployment keeps no history

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max rows (1–1000, default 100).

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Keyset cursor, first half: the last row's `recorded_at`, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

parameters.name: before_id
parameters.description:
Keyset cursor, second half: **the same row's `id`**. Send both. A whole flush of alerts is
written in one transaction and therefore shares one `recorded_at`, so a timestamp-only
cursor lands inside that group and skips its remaining rows. Omitting it is still accepted
and means "strictly before that instant", which is what an older client sends.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description:
Only transitions recorded at or after this RFC 3339 timestamp.

Bounds `recorded_at` (when the row was written), not `at_unix_ms` (when the alert fired), so
one index serves the ordering, the cursor and the range. The two differ by the ingest
writer's flush latency — under a second — so a row may sit marginally outside the window its
displayed time suggests.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description:
Only transitions recorded at or before this RFC 3339 timestamp. Bounds `recorded_at`; see
`since`.

parameters.name: severity
parameters.description:
Comma-separated severities (`info`, `warning`, `critical`); empty or absent means every
severity. An unknown token is rejected rather than ignored — a dropped token would silently
widen the answer to everything.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Comma-separated node states; empty or absent means every state.

parameters.name: resolved
parameters.description: `false` for fires only, `true` for clears only. Omit for both.

parameters.name: acked
parameters.description:
`true` for transitions whose incident has been acknowledged, `false` for those that have
not. Omit for both. Acknowledgement is per incident (node + check + severity), so every
transition of one incident answers the same way.

parameters.name: metric
parameters.description:
Only transitions whose metric name contains this text (case-insensitive). Liveness rows
store no metric and therefore never match.

parameters.name: node_id
parameters.description:
Only transitions about this node. Rows about something other than a node (a poller pool)
are excluded by construction.

parameters.name: node_q
parameters.description:
Only transitions about nodes whose **current name** contains this text (case-insensitive).
Distinct from `node_id`, which names exactly one node.

parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description: Only transitions about nodes in this folder group **or any group beneath it**.

200.description: A page of history rows, newest first; empty when this deployment keeps no history

400.description: A cursor or range bound is not RFC 3339, or `severity`/`state` is not one of the listed values

404.description: The requested `node_id` or `group_id` is outside the caller's scope

get.summary: Nodes generating the most alert fires over a trailing window (chronic offenders).

200.description: Nodes ranked by alert fires; empty when this deployment keeps no history, and `partial` says the scope filter may have shortened the list

get.summary: Recent up/down transitions (latest fires and resolutions), node names joined.
get.description:
Only `limit` is documented, though the handler borrows the history query type: this endpoint
reads no cursor, and advertising one would promise paging it does not do.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many transitions to return (default 12)

200.description: The latest fires and resolutions; empty when this deployment keeps no history

get.summary: Findings across every run — the WebUI's All-findings screen.
get.description:
Complements `GET /analysis/jobs/{id}/findings`, which answers "what did this run find". This one
answers the question an operator actually starts from — "has anything been found about this node
/ this site / this week" — which no single run can answer because the runs are what get
enumerated otherwise.

Skeleton mode has no job store, so it answers an empty list rather than a 503: the screen is a
search, and an error where "nothing yet" is the truthful answer reads as a broken page.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Page cursor: the `at` of the previous page's last row (RFC 3339).

parameters.name: before_id
parameters.description:
Page cursor tiebreak: that same row's `id`. Findings written by one run share a millisecond
routinely, so a cursor without it would repeat or skip the rows sharing the boundary
instant. Omitting it reads as "strictly before this instant".

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on finding time, RFC 3339 — the range filter, not the cursor.

parameters.name: tool
parameters.description:
Comma-separated diagnostics (`AnalysisTool` tokens, e.g. `anomaly,capacity`); empty or
absent means every tool. An unknown token is rejected rather than ignored.

parameters.name: severity
parameters.description: Comma-separated severities (`crit`, `warn`, `info`); empty or absent means every severity.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Case-insensitive substring of the metric name **or** the finding kind — the two halves the
*What* column shows.

parameters.name: node_id
parameters.description: Restrict to findings about one node.

parameters.name: node_q
parameters.description:
Case-insensitive substring of the node's current name. Distinct from `node_id`, which names
exactly one node; fleet-wide findings never match this.

parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description: Restrict to findings about nodes in one folder group **and everything beneath it**.

parameters.name: min_score
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on the finding's score. One-sided is the usual shape — "8 or worse".

parameters.name: max_score
parameters.description: Inclusive upper bound on the finding's score.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, clamped to 200 (default 100).

200.description: Matching findings, newest first; empty when this deployment has no runner

400.description: A cursor or range bound is not RFC 3339, or the tool/severity is unknown

404.description: The requested node or group filter is outside the caller's scope

get.summary: Recent analysis jobs (the runs list). `?limit=` (default 50), optionally narrowed.
get.description:
Skeleton mode has no runner, so this answers an empty list rather than a 503: the runs list is
a panel on a page that otherwise works, and an error there would break the page. **The filter is
validated before that early return**, so a malformed one is a 400 on every deployment rather
than an empty `200` on some — a client bug that reads as "no runs" is worse than an error.

parameters.name: tool
parameters.description: Only runs of this analysis (e.g. `anomaly`).

parameters.name: state
parameters.description:
Only runs in this state: `queued` | `running` | `done` | `failed` | `cancelled`.
Note `done`, not `succeeded` — that is the report-run vocabulary, not this one.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only runs started at or after this instant (RFC 3339).

200.description: Matching runs, newest first; empty when this deployment has no runner

400.description: The tool or state is outside its vocabulary, or `since` is not RFC 3339

get.summary: Every issued personal access token, as metadata.
get.description:
Neither the raw token nor its hash is returned — a token's value exists only in the response
that created it. These credentials authenticate whichever surfaces each token names — `/mcp`,
this REST API, or both.

200.description: Token metadata only — never the raw token or its hash

503.description: Skeleton mode has no token store

post.summary: Mint a personal access token.
post.description:
The raw token is in this response and nowhere else — only its hash is stored, so no later call
can produce it again.

The token acts as an **account** (`owner_user_id`, defaulting to the caller): disabling or
deleting that account stops the token, and its role is capped at the owner's current role on
every use. For anything unattended, own it with a service account rather than a person — see
`POST /api/v1/users` — so the credential does not depend on who happened to create it.

201.description: Token minted; `token` is the raw bearer and is returned only here

400.description: Bad name, a scope naming no groups or a group that does not exist, a scope on a token whose owner is itself group-scoped, no surface named, an expiry already in the past, or an owner id that names no account

409.description: An API token with that name already exists

503.description: Skeleton mode has no token store

delete.summary: Revoke a personal access token, so it stops authenticating every surface immediately.
delete.description:
Idempotent: a missing or already-revoked id answers `204` too. Revocation is what an operator
reaches for when a token may be compromised, so "it was already gone" is success, not `404`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: API token id

204.description: Token revoked; idempotent, so an already-revoked id also answers 204

503.description: Skeleton mode has no token store

get.summary: The audit log as CSV, narrowed by the same filters as the list.
get.description:
**This is the endpoint that makes Export mean what it says.** The button used to write out the
rows the browser had scrolled to, which is a different set from "everything matching" — in a log
whose purpose is completeness, that is a correctness problem rather than a missing feature. The
list endpoint's filters moved into SQL first; this closes the other half.

`before` is deliberately **not** accepted: a cursor is where a page starts, and an export is not
paged. Accepting it would let a caller export "the second page" and believe it was the answer.

The response is a download rather than JSON, so a failure has nowhere useful to render — which
is why the filter is validated the same way the list validates it, before anything is fetched.

post.summary: Exchange a username and password for a bearer token.
post.description:
Takes `Admin` with no permission guard in front of it — unlike every other handler — because
there is nothing to authenticate yet. A skeleton deployment answering 503 here is correct and
not a disclosure: "there is no user store" is exactly what a would-be logger-in needs to know.

200.description: A bearer token and the role it carries

401.description: Incorrect username or password — one code for both, so the endpoint is not an account-enumeration oracle

429.description: Too many attempts; `Retry-After` carries the wait in seconds

503.description: Skeleton mode has no user store, so there is nothing to log in to

post.summary: Revoke the caller's bearer token so it cannot be reused.
post.description:
Idempotent and unguarded: an absent, expired or already-revoked token still answers 204. Making
logout require a valid session would mean the one action that fixes a suspect token is refused
precisely when the token has gone bad.

204.description: Token revoked; an absent, expired or already-revoked token answers 204 too

get.summary: Report whether every stored credential can still be decrypted.
get.description:
This is the check a restore cannot skip. A database can come back whole — right row counts,
healthy API — while the key-encryption key is a different one, in which case every credential is
permanently unreadable and nothing says so until the next poll fails. `scripts/yagra-restore-verify.sh`
asserts on this endpoint for exactly that reason, and it is worth looking at after any KEK
rotation or restore.

It decrypts in memory and reports booleans; no secret value crosses this boundary.

200.description: Per-credential decryptability. `failures` is empty on a healthy deployment

get.summary: Addresses seen on the network that Yagra does not monitor.
get.description:
Built from the ARP / IPv6-neighbour caches of the nodes that *are* monitored, so an endpoint
appears here only if some monitored router has spoken to it. Requires the ARP walk to be enabled
(Settings ▸ System settings ▸ Discovery walks); with it off the list is empty, which is an answer
rather than an outage.

`summary.truncated_nodes > 0` means at least one router's cache exceeded its row budget and this
list is a **sample**, not a complete inventory of the segment.

parameters.name: via_node
parameters.description: Only endpoints seen by this node.

parameters.name: include_promoted
parameters.description: Include endpoints that have since become monitored nodes. Default `false`.

post.summary: Promote a discovered endpoint to a monitored node.
post.description:
Builds the same `NewNode` a scan import does and goes through the same writer, so classification
(`sysDescr` → maker/model) happens on the node's first identity probe exactly as it does for any
other node — there is no second creation path to keep in step.

`409` means the address is already an inventory node. That is not a failure of the import so much
as an answer: the endpoint stopped being unmonitored between the list being read and the button
being pressed, and the row is reconciled on the way out so the list stops showing it.

post.summary: Ask the poller running a sweep to stop (ADR-068 Increment 2).
post.description:
`ManageConfig`, the same as starting one: stopping a sweep is the same authority as causing it.

**Answers 200 for a scan this core has no record of, unlike `analysis`'s cancel.** That
asymmetry is deliberate. Scan state is in memory, so a restarted core forgets sweeps its pollers
are still running, and requiring a local record would make exactly those sweeps — the ones an
operator most wants to stop — unstoppable. The `analysis` endpoint 404s because there the
200/404 split answers "is that job running" for any id a caller cares to try; here the id is an
unguessable UUID and the caller already holds `ManageConfig`, so the split would only reveal
whether this process remembers something.

200.description: The stop was published. Not a promise that the sweep stopped — watch the scan's state for that

get.summary: The scans this core is holding, newest first.
get.description:
Exists so a sweep survives leaving the page: the scan id used to live only in the browser tab
that started it, so navigating away lost a sweep the poller was still running. What bounds this
list is the runner's retention (finished scans age out, running ones are never capped away),
not the caller's `limit`.

**A restarted core answers an empty list even while a poller is still sweeping** — scan state is
in memory by decision (ADR-068). That is why the WebUI must render "this core does not know that
scan" for a 404 on a remembered id, rather than an empty page.

`ManageConfig` and `503` in skeleton mode, matching `GET /discovery/scan/{id}` rather than the
candidates queue: this list is the Discovery screen's own state, and a screen that cannot scan
has no scans to list. (The candidates queue answers `200 []` instead because it backs a
dashboard widget, where an error would break a page that otherwise works.)

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Time-range lower bound (inclusive, RFC 3339). Distinct from `before` (the paging cursor).

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: Time-range upper bound (inclusive, RFC 3339).

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description:
Event kinds to include, comma-separated (`syslog,trap`). A single value is the long-standing
spelling and still works; an empty value or an absent parameter means every kind.

parameters.name: matched
parameters.description:
Only rule-matched events (or only unmatched ones). Superseded by `action`, which says *what*
the rule did; kept because it is a narrower question some clients still ask.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Rule outcomes to include, comma-separated (`fired,cleared`); empty or absent means all.

parameters.name: severity
parameters.description:
Syslog severities (0–7) to include, comma-separated; empty or absent means all. An event
with no syslog severity — a trap, a webhook — matches no severity filter.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Free-text matched against source (node name / IP) or message, case-insensitively. Whether
it also matches inside a word depends on the store this deployment searches: PostgreSQL
matches any substring, a log store matches whole words. With `regex`, it is instead a
regular expression matched against the message only, which reaches inside words on either.

parameters.name: regex
parameters.description: Interpret `q` as a regular expression (message-only) rather than a plain term.

parameters.name: msg
parameters.description: Message-only condition, matched with the same store-dependent word rules as `q`.

parameters.name: msg_regex
parameters.description: Interpret `msg` as a regular expression, which reaches inside words on either store.

Inbound ack reflection. An external incident tool mirrors ack state in by the dedup identity
`(subject, check, severity)`; `acked:false` clears it. `AckAlerts`-gated; the mutating-request
middleware records the audit entry.

by.description: External actor reference (id / handle) — never a secret.

node.description:
The node the alert is about. Omit it and send `subject` instead for an alert about
something other than a node (a poller pool). Exactly one of the two is required.

note.description: Optional free-text note from the external tool.

subject.description:
The alert's subject in its flat form — a node's UUID, or `pool:<name>`. This is the value
the alert's own `node` field carries, so an integration can echo back what it received.

AckResult.description: What an ack call reports back: the new state, and the stored view when acknowledging.

AckView.description:
The acknowledgement view attached to an alert / history row in API responses. Carries who
acked it, when, from which external tool, and an optional note. Never carries a secret.

at_unix_ms.description: When the external tool recorded the ack (Unix ms, UTC).

by.description: External actor reference (id / handle) — not a secret.

note.description: Optional free-text note from the external tool.

subject_name.description: The subject's name, for a subject identified by name rather than by id (a poller pool).

ActiveAlertView.description:
An active alert plus its inbound (read-only) ack state.

`subject_kind` and `subject_name` decompose the alert's `node` field, which carries either a
node's UUID or `pool:<name>`. The live alert stream emits the same three keys.

Alert.description: A single alert produced by the engine.

oneOf.description: Numeric breach detail for a threshold alert; `None` for a liveness alert.

flapping.description: Whether the underlying check is currently flapping.

metric.description:
Metric the check measured (e.g. `"icmp_rtt_ms"`; the liveness sentinel for up/down).
Carried for the history log + notification payload so a human can read *what* fired —
not part of alert identity (dedup/grouping ignore it).

node.description: What the alert is about: a node's UUID, or `pool:<name>` for a poller-pool alert.

oneOf.description: Root-cause node, if this alert was attributed upstream by dependency analysis.

state.description: The committed state that triggered the alert.

asked_about.description:
Set when the operator clicked a *symptom* and the context hopped to its cause. Naming the
node they clicked keeps the answer connected to what they were looking at.

oneOf.description: Numeric detail for a threshold alert; absent for liveness.

flapping.description:
Whether the engine is damping this check as flapping. Worth telling the model: a flapping
link and a hard failure have different causes and different next steps.

metric.description: What the check measured — `icmp_rtt_ms`, or the liveness sentinel.

AlertHistoryRow.description: One alert-history row for the API.

oneOf.description: Which way the metric crossed its bound (threshold checks only).

id.description:
This row's identity, and the second half of the keyset cursor — pass it as `before_id`
beside `before`. Also the stable key for a list: no other field, or combination of them, is
unique.

metric.description:
Metric the check measured (e.g. `icmp_rtt_ms`, or the liveness sentinel). `None` for
rows recorded before this was captured (legacy) so the WebUI can show "—".

node.description:
The node this transition was about; `null` when the subject is not a node — read
`subject_kind` first. It is non-null exactly when `subject_kind` is `node`.

observed_value.description: Observed sample value that committed the transition (threshold checks only).

recorded_at.description:
Insertion time as an RFC 3339 timestamp, and the first half of the **keyset cursor**: the
WebUI passes the last row's `recorded_at` as `before` **and its `id` as `before_id`** to
fetch the next (older) page. Distinct from `at_unix_ms` (the event time).

⚠️ Both halves are required, and this is not defensive. `recorded_at` defaults to `now()`,
which in PostgreSQL is the *transaction* timestamp, and [`AlertHistoryStore::record_batch`]
writes a whole flush as one multi-row `INSERT` — so every row of a flush shares a
`recorded_at` to the microsecond. A page boundary landing inside a flush and paging on the
timestamp alone silently **skipped** that flush's remaining rows. A fleet-wide event is
exactly when a flush is large and exactly when someone is reading this log.

subject_name.description: The subject's name, for a subject identified by name rather than by id (a poller pool).

threshold_value.description: The bound crossed for the committed severity (threshold checks only).

AlertHistoryView.description:
An alert-history row plus its current inbound ack state (keyed by the dedup identity, so all
transitions of one incident share it).

AlertTransition.description: One recent state-change row (a fire = into an alert state; a resolve = recovery to ok).

resolved.description: true = recovery (→ ok); false = went into the alert state.

AnalysisFinding.description: One finding produced by an analysis (anomaly card / correlation pair / capacity / flap row).

AnalysisJob.description:
A job row, as served to the API / SSE. Timestamps are epoch-millis so the WebUI formats
relative times without a date dependency.

AnalysisJobState.description:
Where an analysis run is in its lifecycle.

A bare `String` until v0.2.6, and the cost of that was paid twice. The vocabulary had to be
written out by hand at the API edge to validate the runs filter, and again in the WebUI to fill
its dropdown — two lists nothing compared. Worse, `state: string` compares equal to *any*
string: the in-app "your analysis finished" notice tested `state === 'succeeded'`, which is the
**report-run** vocabulary, so every successful analysis announced itself as a failure. Typing it
makes that comparison a compile error on both sides.

AnalysisSchedule.description: A schedule row, as served to the API.

params.description: The launch knobs, the same shape as `AnalysisJob.params`.

tool.description: Which diagnostic runs, as an `AnalysisTool` token.

AnalysisScheduleBody.description: Create/update body for an analysis schedule: the launch spec plus the cadence.

notify.description:
Whether a completed run may notify. Defaults to `false` — a schedule fires unattended, so
silence is the safer default; the manual launch path defaults it on because someone is
waiting for that run.

tool.description: Which diagnostic to run (an `AnalysisTool` token, e.g. `anomaly`).

AnalysisScheduleStatus.description: Outcome of a schedule's most recent firing attempt.

ApiErrorBody.description:
The ADR-019 envelope every failure renders as. `pub(crate)` and schema-bearing so the OpenAPI
document can name one error shape for every endpoint (ADR-035) instead of leaving 4xx/5xx bodies
undescribed — a client that has to guess the failure shape ends up parsing the success shape and
reading `undefined`.

ApiTokenInfo.description:
One API token's metadata for the admin listing — **never** the raw token or its hash. A
credential is not returned in an API response after it has been issued.

expires_at.description: When the token stops authenticating, or `None` for no expiry.

owner.description:
The account the token acts as. `None` means the owner was deleted before this column
existed, or could not be matched during the 0057 backfill — such a token no longer
authenticates and is shown so an admin can revoke it deliberately.

owner_active.description:
Whether the owner account is currently able to authenticate (enabled). Surfaced so the
listing can explain a token that is live by its own dates yet refused.

owner_last_login_at.description:
The owner's last interactive sign-in, when the owner authenticates through an external IdP.
This is the only signal Yagra has that an SSO account is still live (see [`ApiTokenStore`]),
so the listing shows it; `None` for local and service accounts, where it means nothing.

surfaces.description:
Which auth surfaces this token may be presented at. Never empty in practice — a token that
named no surface could authenticate nowhere — but stored as a list so it can grow.

AppSettingsRow.description:
The deployment-wide settings the bundle carries. The retention windows are deliberately absent
(module docs).

ApplyUpgrade.description: A request to move this deployment to a particular release.

target_tag.description:
The release tag to move to, e.g. `v0.2.2`. Must be a published release tag; the repository
it is fetched from is fixed by the deployment and cannot be set here.

AuditAction.description: What an audit entry was, as the log's filterable vocabulary.

AuditRow.description: One audit row (API shape; `at` is RFC 3339 text at the edge).

AuditStatusClass.description: How an audit entry's HTTP status turned out.

scope.description:
Which slice of the inventory this account sees: `"All"`, or the node groups it is limited
to. The UI reads it to say so out loud — an operator looking at a filtered node list has no
other way to tell a narrow scope from a small fleet.

AuthorizeUrl.description: Where to send the browser to start the SSO handshake.

AvailableRelease.description: One release the sidecar found, with the digests it resolved.

core_digest.description: Resolved image digest for `yagra-core` at that tag; `null` when it could not be resolved.

AvailableVersions.description: The versions the sidecar last saw in the registry (`available.json`).

error.description:
Why the list is empty or stale, when the sidecar could not reach the registry. A closed
network has no registry, so this is an ordinary state rather than a fault.

written_at.description: Unix seconds when the list was refreshed.

BodyMatch.description:
A keyword rule applied to a URL monitor's response body.

When present, the monitor reports `http_body_match` (`1` satisfied / `0` not) in addition to
`http_up`. How much of the body is read is [`UrlCheckConfig::body_max_bytes`].

mode.description: Whether the keyword must be present or absent (default: present).

pattern.description: The keyword to look for. Matched as plain, case-sensitive text — not a regular expression.

BodyMatchMode.description: Whether the keyword must be present or absent for the body to be considered healthy.

Breach.description:
Numeric breach detail for a threshold alert (absent for a liveness up/down alert).
Carried for the history log + notification payload — not part of alert identity.

direction.description: Which way the metric crossed its bound.

threshold.description: The bound crossed for the committed severity, if the rule defines one at that level.

value.description: Observed sample value that committed the transition.

BundleNote.description: One note, with the table it concerns and how many rows it covers.

count.description: How many rows this note covers.

field.description: The column involved, when the note is about one (e.g. `credential_id`).

table.description: The table the note is about.

BusCertRegenerate.description: Which names a regenerated bus certificate should cover.

names.description:
Hostnames and IP addresses remote pollers will dial, added to the deployment's internal
defaults. A poller's connection fails unless the exact address it dials is present, so this
is the field that decides whether a new site can connect.

BusRemoteAccepted.description: What the switch returns. The poller secret appears **once**.

ca_certificate.description:
The certificate a remote poller must pin as its `YAGRA_BUS_CA_FILE`, in PEM. `null` when
disabling.

id.description: Identifier for this change, matching the run reported by the upgrade status endpoint.

maintenance_window_id.description:
The fleet-wide maintenance window opened for the duration, or `null` if one could not be
opened. Monitoring stops for as long as the bus is being recreated.

poller_secret.description:
The bootstrap secret a remote poller presents when it connects, shown **once**. Store it
now — it is written into the deployment's environment and is never returned again.

BusRemoteRequest.description: Turn acceptance of remote-site pollers on or off.

enabled.description:
`true` encrypts and authenticates the bus and publishes its port; `false` returns it to the
internal-only plaintext bus and stops every remote poller from connecting.

names.description:
Hostnames and IP addresses remote pollers will dial. Used to reissue the certificate before
the bus restarts, so the names are already right when it comes back. Ignored when disabling.

BusResponse.description: The bus, as Settings ▸ Pollers shows it.

can_switch.description:
Whether the switch below can be operated. `false` means the updater sidecar that performs it
is not deployed, is switched off, or has stopped reporting — the certificate is still
readable, but turning remote acceptance on or off needs a shell on the host.

oneOf.description: The certificate the bus serves, or `null` if none has been established yet.

remote_enabled.description:
Whether this core is talking to the bus over TLS, which is what accepting remote-site
pollers requires.

BusTlsView.description: The bus certificate as the settings card shows it. Never includes the private key.

certificate.description:
The certificate in PEM. This is what a remote poller uses as its `YAGRA_BUS_CA_FILE` — a
self-signed certificate is its own certificate authority. Safe to distribute; the private
key never leaves the server.

expires_in_days.description: Days until expiry; negative once it has passed.

fingerprint_sha256.description:
Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the certificate. Compare it against the file a site was given to
confirm the site is holding this certificate and not an older one.

issued_at.description: When this certificate was generated, RFC 3339.

issued_by.description:
The account that asked for it, if a signed-in user did. Empty for the one generated
automatically before the bus first started.

issuer.description:
Distinguished name of the issuer. Equal to `subject`, because this certificate is
self-signed.

key_algorithm.description: Key type and size, for example `ECDSA P-256`.

key_unreadable.description:
Whether the private key can still be decrypted. `false` means the encryption key has changed
or been lost, and a new certificate has to be generated — which every remote site must then
be given.

materialized.description:
Whether the files the bus reads match this certificate. `false` means it is stored but has
not reached the volume yet — the bus is still serving whatever it started with.

not_after.description: End of the validity window, RFC 3339.

not_before.description: Start of the validity window, RFC 3339.

sans.description:
The hostnames and IP addresses this certificate is valid for. A remote poller's connection
fails unless the exact address it dials appears here.

subject.description: Distinguished name of the certificate's subject.

CancelRequested.description:
The outcome of asking a sweep to stop.

⚠️ **Deliberately does not claim the sweep stopped**, and the field names carry that. Core
broadcasts the stop and cannot know who — or whether anyone — acted on it, so the honest report
is "requested, and here is whether the pollers that might be running it understand the command".
The confirmation arrives later, as the scan's own state going to `cancelled`.

poller_supports_cancel.description:
Whether every live poller that could be running this sweep advertises cancellation support.

⚠️ An **approximation**, which is why it is not called `will_stop`. A sweep on the global
route could be held by any live poller, so this is the answer across all of them; even for a
pool-scoped sweep it says the pool can stop sweeps, not that the poller holding this one
will. `false` means at least one poller predates the feature and the sweep may run to
completion.

pool.description: The pool the stop was published to; `null` for the global subject.

requested.description: The stop was published. Always true on a 200 — a publish failure is a 500.

Candidate.description: One device a scan found, with a suggested profile for the operator to confirm on import.

matched_credential_id.description:
The stored credential that answered SNMP, by reference (never the value) — the UI
preselects it on import so the working secret is bound automatically.

suggested_profile_id.description:
Suggested device profile, resolved **server-side** via the classification rules (by
sysObjectID prefix, else sysDescr regex, else "Generic SNMP" when SNMP answered). An id,
not a name, so the UI binds it robustly even if the profile was renamed.

sysobjectid.description:
`sysObjectID` (dotted) if it answered SNMP — the authoritative device-type signal the
classifier prefers. Shown to the operator and useful for authoring rules.

vendor.description:
Maker / model best-effort parsed from sysDescr (editable on import) — pre-fills the
node's descriptive metadata so the imported node displays "name (addr) (vendor) (model)".

action.description: `"{METHOD} {path}"`, as recorded by the audit middleware.

oneOf.description:
JSM Alerts / Opsgenie-compatible API. `api_url` is the integration base
(e.g. `https://api.atlassian.com/jsm/ops/integration/v2`); `api_key` is the
GenieKey (a secret).

ChannelConfig.description: The (secret) connection config for a channel — sealed at rest, never returned by the API.

ChannelSummary.description: Channel metadata for the API — never the secret config.

body_template.description: Template for the notification body. Absent means Yagra's built-in format is used.

subject_template.description: Template for the notification subject. Absent means Yagra's built-in wording is used.

CheckId.description:
Stable identifier for a single check on a node (e.g. "icmp liveness", a specific
threshold). Part of the alert dedup key `(node, check, severity)`.

ClassificationRule.description:
A persisted rule mapping a device signature to a profile. At least one of
`sysobjectid_prefix` / `sysdescr_regex` is set (the DB enforces this with a CHECK).

enabled.description: Disabled rules are skipped during classification.

priority.description: Evaluation order: ascending, lowest first. Most-specific rules get lower numbers.

profile_id.description: The profile to suggest when this rule matches.

sysdescr_regex.description:
Match when the device's `sysDescr` matches this regular expression — a fallback for
devices whose `sysObjectID` isn't covered by a prefix rule.

sysobjectid_prefix.description:
Match when the device's `sysObjectID` starts with this dotted-OID prefix
(e.g. `1.3.6.1.4.1.9.` for Cisco). Authoritative — preferred over `sysDescr`.

vendor.description:
Optional vendor/model to pre-fill on the import row (overrides the `sysDescr`
heuristic when set). Descriptive metadata only — never a TSDB label.

ClassificationRuleBody.description: Create/update body. At least one of `sysobjectid_prefix` / `sysdescr_regex` must be present.

ClearedWindows.description: The outcome of a bulk clear.

deleted.description:
How many windows were deleted. May be lower than a client expected: the server's clock
decides what has ended, and a group-scoped caller clears only what it can see.

auth_available.description: Whether interactive login exists at all (false in skeleton mode).

flow_enabled.description:
Whether this deployment has a traffic-flow store configured (ADR-031). When `false`, the
flow analyses cannot be scheduled — `POST /api/v1/analysis/schedules` refuses them.

public_dashboard.description: Whether read endpoints are open to anonymous callers.

rca_enabled.description: Whether an LLM provider is configured *and* enabled.

CollectionItem.description:
One thing to collect: a stable metric name, the OID to collect it from, how to collect
it (scalar GET vs table walk), and whether it is a gauge or a raw counter.

metric_kind.description:
Gauge vs raw counter — rates/utilization are derived at query time (ADR-012),
never by the poller.

metric_name.description:
Stable TSDB metric name (e.g. `if_hc_in_octets`). Bounded by convention to keep
label cardinality controlled — never a free-text/device-supplied value (ADR-011).

oid.description:
Dotted OID: a scalar instance OID ([`CollectionKind::Scalar`]) or a table column
base ([`CollectionKind::Table`], the walk root).

CollectionKind.description: How a [`CollectionItem`] is collected from the agent.

CollectionTemplateItemRow.description: One metric inside a collection template.

CompatFloor.description: The oldest core version that can still run this database, and which migration decided that.

min_core.description: Oldest core version that can start against this schema, as bare semver (`"0.3.0"`).

reason.description: Why that migration narrowed the schema.

since_version.description: The migration that imposed the floor.

Condition.description:
One `field op value` test. `value` is always a string so the config has a single JSON shape;
[`compile`] parses it according to the field's type.

value.description: The operand, parsed per field type at compile time.

format.description: Always `yagra.config-bundle`. An importer refuses anything else rather than guessing.

notes.description: What the export left out or changed. Informational; ignored on import.

secrets.description: How secrets are represented. Always `references` — a bundle never carries one.

yagra_version.description: The Yagra version that produced it.

CreateAnalysisJob.description: Request body to launch an analysis (launch drawer / report config bar).

expires_at.description:
When the token stops working. Omit for no expiry — appropriate for a service account driving
an integration, and deliberately still allowed.

owner_user_id.description:
The account the token acts as. Omit to own it yourself; name a service account for anything
unattended, so the credential outlives whoever set it up.

role.description:
The role the token grants (`viewer` is the right default for a read-only client). Capped at
the owner's role on every use, so this is a ceiling rather than a promise.

oneOf.description:
Visibility scope; defaults to `All` when omitted. A group scope limits the token to those
node groups and everything beneath them. It must name groups that exist, and the owner must
itself be unscoped — a token owned by a group-scoped account inherits that account's scope,
so giving it a different one is refused rather than silently ignored.

surfaces.description:
Which surfaces the token may authenticate. Defaults to `["mcp"]` when omitted, matching what
every token issued before this field existed can do.

CreateChannel.description: Create-channel body: a name plus the (secret-bearing) connection config, tagged by `kind`.

CreateCollectionItem.description: Create body for a collection item — the same shape whether it lands on a node or a template.

CreateCredential.description: Create body. `secret` is sealed before storage and never logged.

CreateDnsMonitor.description:
The check config is spelled out rather than `#[serde(flatten)]`ed (as [`CreateUrlMonitor`]
does) because both the node and the check have a `name`: flattening would bind them to the same
JSON key and silently force the display label to equal the resolved name.

CreateRule.description: Create-rule body: a name, an optional severity filter (absent = any), and target channels.

CreateUrlMonitor.description:
`name`/`parent_id`/`pool` plus a flattened [`UrlCheckConfig`] (only `url` is required;
everything else defaults).

CreateUser.description: Create-user request body. The password is hashed before storage and never logged.

oneOf.description:
What kind of account this is. Defaults to `local`, so a client written before service
accounts existed keeps creating exactly what it did before.

`oidc` is not accepted: those accounts are provisioned by signing in through the IdP, never
by hand — creating one here would produce an account whose subject matches nobody.

password.description:
Required for a `local` account, and rejected for a `service` one — a machine account has no
password by design, so accepting a discarded one would advertise a login that does not exist.

CreateWindow.description:
Create-window body. Times are RFC 3339; the scope mirrors thresholds (ADR-013) plus
`group_id` (a folder-group UUID, resolved recursively — the All Nodes right-click scope).

CreatedApiToken.description:
The one and only response carrying a usable token.

A named type rather than an inline `json!` because of what the `token` field is: the client has
to store it now, since only its hash is kept and no later call can produce it again. Giving it a
type makes that field visible in one place if this response ever grows a second consumer.

token.description: The raw bearer token, returned **once**. Never stored, never logged.

CreatedId.description:
The id of a freshly created resource — the whole body of a `201`.

Deliberately one shape for every creator. The `json!({"id": …})` literal it replaces was written
out per handler, which is how `{"id": …}` and `{"node_id": …}` both ended up in this API for the
same idea; a client then needs to know which creator it called to read the id back.

CreatedSource.description:
A newly created source, with its ingest token.

**The plaintext token appears here and nowhere else** — only its hash is stored, so this response
and `rotate-token` are the only two places it can ever be read.

CredentialHealth.description: Whether the stored credentials can actually be decrypted with the KEK this process loaded.

decryptable.description: How many of them the current key opened successfully.

failures.description:
The ones that failed, if any. A non-empty list means polling with those credentials will
fail until the correct key file is restored.

CredentialId.description: Stable identifier for a stored monitoring credential (SNMP community / v3 / token).

CredentialSummary.description: Credential metadata returned by the API — never includes the secret value.

used_by.description:
How many nodes reference this credential — answers "is it safe to delete?". Counted at
list time from `nodes.credential_id`; `0` means the credential is unused.

CurrentNeighbors.description: A node's current adjacency and how long it has held.

first_seen.description: When this exact set was first seen (RFC 3339).

last_seen.description: When it was last confirmed unchanged (RFC 3339).

neighbors.description: The adjacencies the node last reported.

DashboardSaved.description: A save's acknowledgement. The layout is not echoed back — the client already has it.

DependencyHealth.description:
Reachability of one backing dependency. Carries only a boolean and a human label — no connection
strings, no secrets.

Dependents.description: Alerts attributed upstream to this incident.

named.description: The named dependents, capped — see `total` for how many there actually are.

total.description: How many there are in total — kept separately so truncation is visible rather than silent.

DestKind.description: How a destination is spoken to.

DestStatus.description: A destination's runtime status, as the API serializes it.

circuit_open.description: Whether the circuit breaker is currently open (sends are being dropped fast).

dropped.description: Messages dropped without being sent (full queue, rate cap, or open circuit).

last_success_unix_ms.description: Last successful send, Unix ms; `None` if there has not been one.

queue_depth.description: Messages currently queued for this destination.

rendered.description: Messages sent re-rendered because no raw payload was available, despite `verbatim`.

Direction.description: Which way a metric breaches its bound.

DiscoveredEndpointCursor.description: Keyset cursor for the next page.

DiscoveredEndpointPage.description: One page of discovered endpoints, most recently seen first.

oneOf.description: Pass back as `before_last_seen`+`before_id`; `null` ⇒ this was the last page.

DiscoveredEndpointRow.description: One address the fleet has resolved on the wire but does not monitor.

first_seen.description: When it was first seen anywhere in the fleet (RFC 3339).

last_seen.description: When it was last confirmed still present (RFC 3339).

mac.description: Its hardware address, lowercase colon-separated hex; `null` for an incomplete ARP entry.

promoted_node_id.description: The node this address became, once it is monitored; `null` while it is still unmonitored.

via_ifindex.description: The SNMP ifIndex it was resolved on — the port it is behind.

via_node.description: Which monitored node resolved it; `null` once that node has been deleted.

DiscoveredEndpointSummary.description: How much of the fleet's ARP data this list was built from.

nodes_reporting.description: How many nodes have reported an ARP/ND cache at all.

observed_total.description: Total endpoints observed across the fleet, before dedup and before the unmonitored filter.

truncated_nodes.description: How many of those hit a cap, making their contribution a sample rather than a total.

DiscoveryScanState.description:
Where a scan is in its life (ADR-068).

Deliberately has **no `Unknown` variant**, unlike the enums built by `stored_enum::token_enum!`:
those degrade a token a *newer writer* put in a database column, and this value is never read
back from storage — it only ever travels outward. The corresponding defensiveness lives on the
TypeScript side, which narrows the wire value and renders anything it does not recognise
neutrally. ⚠️ Rendering an unrecognised state as a failure is a real bug this codebase has
already shipped once (report runs, painted red by a `switch` with a `default:` arm).

DiskUsage.description:
Usage of one watched filesystem (or a store-size proxy, e.g. the PostgreSQL database size which
core cannot `statvfs`). `size_bytes == 0` means "total capacity unknown" — the value is a bare
growing size (used only), not a fraction of a disk.

mount.description:
Friendly mount label (e.g. `root`, `metrics`, `database`) — a stable, low-cardinality name,
never a raw device path, so it is safe as a TSDB label.

size_bytes.description: Total filesystem capacity in bytes; `0` when unknown (capacity not measurable).

used_bytes.description: Bytes in use on the filesystem (or the store's size when `size_bytes == 0`).

DnsAnswer.description:
One answer record plus its TTL.

The TTL is **display-only**: it counts down between polls, so including it in the content key
would make every single poll register as a change.

ttl.description: Time-to-live as reported by the resolver, in seconds.

DnsChain.description:
One observed resolution chain — the artifact of a DNS check.

Produced by the transport, carried on `PollResult.dns_chain`, persisted to PostgreSQL. **Never
a TSDB label** (ADR-011); it is the same tier as the interface inventory and `sys_descr`.

oneOf.description: `None` ⇒ resolved. A failed chain may still carry hops (e.g. one CNAME, then NXDOMAIN).

hops.description: The hops in walk order. Order is significant and is never sorted.

resolve_ms.description: Total wall-clock milliseconds for the walk. **Not** part of the content key.

resolver.description:
Where we asked, rendered for display (e.g. `10.0.0.53:53` or `system`). Provenance, **not**
content: swapping resolvers while the answer stays the same is not a change.

DnsChainCurrent.description: The node's current resolution chain, plus how long it has held.

DnsChainHistory.description: One page of chain changes, newest first.

oneOf.description: Pass back as `before_at`+`before_id` for the next page; `null` ⇒ this was the last one.

DnsCheckConfig.description: A node's DNS-monitoring configuration (1:1 with the node).

max_depth.description: Maximum CNAME hops before giving up (default 8).

name.description: The name to resolve, e.g. `horryworks.net`. Stored normalized (lowercase, no trailing dot).

record_type.description: Which record type the chain must reach (default `A`).

resolver.description: Recursive resolver to query. `None` ⇒ the poller container's system resolver.

timeout_ms.description: **Total** budget for the whole chain walk, in milliseconds (default 3000).

DnsCheckRow.description: A DNS monitor's configuration (1:1 with its node).

oneOf.description: Authoritative "no such name" (RCODE 3).
NOERROR, but no record of the requested type and no CNAME to follow.
The resolver failed to answer the question (RCODE 2).
The resolver refused to answer (RCODE 5).
Any other response code, kept numeric so a new RCODE is never lost.
The resolver did not answer within the check's budget.
A CNAME pointed at a name already visited in this chain.

at.description: The name the loop closed on.

oneOf.description: The chain was longer than the configured `max_depth`.
The response could not be decoded or did not match the question asked.

DnsFailure.description: Why a resolution did not reach a terminal record set.

DnsFailureKind.description:
Why a resolution failed, without the detail that distinguishes one instance from another — the
`failure_kind` column, and what the API serves for grouping.

DnsHistoryCursor.description: Keyset cursor for the next page (ADR-019 — never OFFSET).

DnsHop.description: One hop of a resolution chain: the name asked about and the answers that came back for it.

answers.description: The answers whose owner is `name`, canonicalized (sorted, deduped, capped).

name.description: The name queried at this hop (normalized).

oneOf.description: A CNAME alias target (normalized: lowercase, no trailing dot).

target.description: The name this hop is an alias for.

oneOf.description: An IPv4 address record.
An IPv6 address record.

DnsRecord.description:
One record in an answer set.

Typed rather than a rendered `String` so ordering is **numeric**: `Ipv4Addr`'s `Ord` compares
octets, so `9.9.9.9` sorts before `10.1.2.3`. Text ordering gets that backwards, which would
make the canonical form depend on how the resolver happened to rotate a round-robin RRset.

DnsRecordType.description:
Which record type a DNS check resolves to. Stored as an UPPERCASE token (the `record_type`
column).

`Cname` is a legitimate terminal type: it answers "what is this name an alias for?" without
chasing on to an address.

EnabledBody.description:
The body of an enable/disable toggle — `{"enabled": true}`.

Shared rather than per-domain because it already was: the maintenance module reached across for
`super::EnabledBody` while it was declared inside the notifications block, which is the same
cross-domain reach that keeps turning up as a migration tripwire.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code. Clients branch on this, never on the message.

message.description: Operator-facing sentence. Safe to display; never carries an internal error's own text.

EventAction.description:
What the pipeline did with an event. When several rules match one event, the row records the
strongest outcome.

EventKind.description: What kind of passive event a poller (or core, for webhooks) received.

EventMatchKind.description: How a rule's pattern is matched against the event text.

EventRow.description: One received event, as served by `GET /api/v1/events`.

trap_name.description:
Well-known MIB name for `trap_oid` (e.g. `linkDown`), derived at read time; `None`
for syslog/webhook events or an OID outside the curated set.

EventRuleTest.description: Body for the interactive rule tester.

EventSearchSemantics.description:
How a plain (non-regex) search term matches on this deployment. Which one applies depends on
the store that answers event searches, so a client that wants a term to behave the same
everywhere should use a regular expression instead.

EventSourceView.description: A webhook ingest source, as served by the API (never includes the token hash).

EventStatBucket.description:
One categorical `/events/stats` bucket: a stable `key` (for the React key + fallback display), an
optional display `label` resolved server-side (e.g. a trap's MIB name), an optional `node_id`
(set for source grouping when the source maps to an inventory node, so the UI resolves its name
— no raw UUID rule), and the row count.

oneOf.description: `group_by=time`: the volume series.
Every other `group_by`: count-ordered categorical buckets.

EventStats.description:
The two row shapes `/events/stats` answers with, as one type.

`#[serde(untagged)]`, so the bytes are exactly the bare array either arm used to serialize on its
own — the union exists because a `Response` names no shape at all in the generated contract, and
a client that has to guess between two arrays guesses wrong on one of them.

EventTimeBucket.description:
One time bucket for the `/events/stats?group_by=time` volume series: a bucket-start timestamp
(Unix ms), the total count, and — when `split=kind` — the per-kind breakdown.

ExemptionBody.description: Whether a node is released from the suppression it inherits.

exempt.description:
`true` releases the node until the coverage it was carved out of ends. `false` puts it
back, and is accepted whether or not it was released — this is a state, not a toggle.

ExemptionKind.description:
Which kind of suppression a node has been released from.

⚠️ Not [`yagra_common::Node`]'s `suppression_opt_out` (migration 0069), which is about *derived
dependency* suppression (ADR-043). This is about maintenance windows and mutes, and the two must
not be wired to each other.

oneOf.description: Any 2xx (the default).
An explicit set of acceptable codes.
An inclusive range `[lo, hi]`.

ExpectedStatus.description:
Which HTTP status codes count as "up". Serialized as a tagged object (the `expected_status`
JSONB column), e.g. `{"kind":"two_xx"}` / `{"kind":"exact","codes":[200,204]}`.

FilterExpr.description: A destination's filter as stored and edited. `{}` deserializes to "match everything".

conditions.description: The conditions; empty means match everything.

FilterOp.description: What a condition does with the datum.

FleetCoverage.description: Fleet data-coverage summary: fresh vs total nodes + the stale watchlist.

coverage_pct.description: Percent of nodes reporting fresh data (100 when the inventory is empty).

stale.description:
The stale nodes by name, capped at [`STALE_WATCHLIST_MAX`]; `total - fresh` is the real
count, so a truncated list is still legible against the totals above it.

FleetGroupSummary.description: The per-group rollup response: `group_id → direct-member state counts`.

FleetStateHistory.description: Node-state counts over time, pivoted into per-state series on a shared timestamp axis.

series.description:
One aligned series per state. Keyed off [`NodeState::ALL`], so every state is present with
zeroes even if it never occurred in the window — the chart's series set must not change
shape depending on what happened to the fleet.

FleetSummary.description:
Total node count plus a per-state tally.

The `states` keys are **always all six** and always sum to `total`, so a client can index them
blind. Shared with the MCP `get_fleet_summary` tool, which used to build its own version that
omitted zeroes.

FlowAsAgg.description:
An autonomous-system aggregate. `asn = 0` means unknown (the UI labels it accordingly). `name`
is resolved from the IP→ASN table at the API layer (the store leaves it `None`).

FlowConversation.description:
A conversation: a src→dst pair with summed traffic. `src_asn`/`dst_asn` are the stored
per-flow AS numbers (0 = unknown); the `*_as_name` fields are resolved from the IP→ASN table
at the API layer (the store leaves them `None`), mirroring [`FlowAsAgg`].

dst_as_name.description: Destination AS organization name, if resolvable (filled at the API layer).

src_as_name.description: Source AS organization name, if resolvable (filled at the API layer).

FlowPoint.description: A trend point: bytes/packets for one protocol at one 5-minute bucket.

FlowTalker.description: A top-talker: one host address with summed traffic.

addr.description: Host address (v4 or v6, normalized from ClickHouse's v4-mapped form).

ForwardDestination.description: A destination as the API exposes it — no secrets, ever.

ca_cert.description:
Extra PEM certificate(s) trusted for a TLS destination, on top of the system roots. Not a
secret — a CA certificate is public — so it round-trips through the API like any other field.

dest_kind.description: How the collector is spoken to.

enabled.description: Whether the forwarder currently sends to it.

filter.description: The filter; `{}` forwards the whole stream.

has_secret.description: Whether a sealed secret is stored (so the UI can show "configured" without revealing it).

pool.description: Restrict to one poller pool; `None` = every pool.

verbatim.description: `true` = relay original bytes, `false` = rebuild from parsed fields.

ForwardDestinationBody.description: Request body for creating/updating a forwarding destination.

ca_cert.description:
PEM certificate(s) to trust for a TLS destination, in addition to the system roots. Not a
secret, so unlike `community` it round-trips and an empty value clears it.

community.description:
SNMP community for re-encoded traps (`snmp_trap_udp` only). Sealed at rest; on update,
omitting it keeps the stored value.

dest_kind.description: How to speak to the collector.

enabled.description: Whether the forwarder should send to it. Defaults to enabled.

filter.description: The filter; omitted = forward the whole stream.

pool.description: Restrict to one poller pool; omitted/null = every pool.

service_account_json.description:
Google service-account key JSON for a `bigquery` destination. Sealed at rest; on update,
omitting it keeps the stored key. Omitting it on create selects Workload Identity (the
GCE/GKE metadata server), which stores no secret at all.

verbatim.description: Relay the original bytes (default) rather than re-rendering from the parsed fields.

ForwardDestinationRow.description:
A forwarding destination. Its optional sealed secret is not carried; a destination that had one
arrives disabled.

had_secret.description:
Whether the source deployment had a sealed secret on this destination. Carries no secret —
it is what tells the importer to arrive disabled and what tells the operator to re-enter it.

destinations.description: Runtime counters, one entry per running destination.

pollers_without_flow_relay.description:
Online pollers that relay no flow datagrams at all, so a flow destination fed only by these
receives nothing.

pollers_without_raw_capture.description: Online pollers that cannot attach the original bytes, so their traffic degrades to rendered.

sending.description: False on an HA standby, whose dispatcher is not running (destination CRUD still works).

GeoSource.description: Where a group's effective map position came from.

GroupBody.description: Create/update body for a group. `group_type` is a validated [`GroupType`] key.

Poll-pool this folder assigns to its nodes (ADR-009/020). Same three-state contract as a
node's: **absent** leaves it unchanged, `""` clears it (inherit from the nearest ancestor,
else the default pool), otherwise it moves the folder's nodes to that pool.

GroupGeo.description: A folder's map pin. Both fields or neither — see [`set_node_group_geo`].

GroupNodes.description:
One group's direct members. Not keyset-paged — a folder is loaded whole when it is expanded —
so it reports truncation instead of offering a cursor.

GroupPlacement.description:
Drag-reorder a group: re-parent it under `parent_id` (`null` ⇒ top level) and position it
relative to a sibling. `before`/`after` name the sibling; both omitted ⇒ append.

GroupStateCounts.description:
Per-group direct-member state tally. All six keys are always present (a missing state is `0`)
and they sum to the group's direct-member count.

GroupSummary.description: One group row returned by the API. `group_type` is the snake_case key.

effective_latitude.description:
Where this group sits on the map after inheritance: its own coordinates, else the nearest
ancestor's, else null. Computed on every read; never stored.

**These do not add a pin.** A group is drawn on the map only when `geo_source` is `own`;
for every other group this says which pin its nodes are counted at (`geo_group`).

geo_group.description:
The group that supplied the effective position: this group when `geo_source` is `own`, the
ancestor it inherited from when `inherited`, null when `unset`. This is the pin the group's
nodes belong to, so a client never has to walk the folder tree itself.

geo_source.description: Whether the effective position is the group's own, inherited from an ancestor, or absent.

latitude.description:
The group's own geo coordinates, as stored (both set ⇒ drawn as a pin). A descendant
folder normally leaves these null and inherits — see the `effective_*` pair below.

pool.description:
Poll-pool this folder assigns to its nodes (ADR-009/020, migration 0054). `null` ⇒ inherit
from the nearest ancestor that sets one, else the default pool. A node's own `pool` still
wins — see [`crate::poolres`].

sort_order.description: Manual order within the parent scope (the UI sorts siblings by this, then by name).

HostDiskRange.description:
A per-mount filesystem trend. The frontend derives % from the pair, or shows a bare-bytes trend
when `size_bytes` is all zero (the `database` size proxy has no capacity).

HostInfo.description:
One self-monitored host: current resource values for the core process's host (`role="core"`) or
a poller's (`role="poller"`).

cpu_pct.description: Current CPU utilization % (0–100); `null` when no sample yet.

disk_used_pct.description: Highest watched-filesystem used %, for at-a-glance columns; `null` when none has a capacity.

load1.description: Current 1-minute load average; `null` when no sample / unavailable on the platform.

mem_total_bytes.description: Total physical memory, bytes; `null` when no sample.

mem_used_bytes.description: Memory in use, bytes; `null` when no sample.

mem_used_pct.description: Memory-used %, derived; `null` when total is unknown.

online.description:
Whether the source is currently reporting (core is always online; a poller within its
heartbeat window).

pool.description: Pool the poller serves; `null` for core.

HostMetricRange.description:
The scalar host trends plus a per-mount filesystem trend, all over one window — one round trip
per instance/range change.

HttpMethod.description: HTTP request method for a URL check. Stored as an UPPERCASE token (the `method` column).

ImportDiscovered.description: Import body: the selected devices to create as nodes.

ImportEndpoint.description: What to call the endpoint, and what to bind it to, when promoting it to a node.

name.description: Node name. Defaults to the address when omitted or blank.

ImportNode.description: One discovered device the operator chose to add.

vendor.description: Maker/model pre-filled from discovery's sysDescr classification (editable before import).

dry_run.description: True when nothing was committed: the whole import ran and was rolled back.

notes.description: What was skipped or changed, and why.

ImportResult.description: How many nodes an import created.

IncidentContext.description:
Exactly what the model was shown about the incident, so an answer can be checked rather than
trusted (ADR-029). Stored beside the answer; also what makes a bad answer reviewable later.

dependents.description: Alerts rolled up under this one.

generated_at_s.description:
When the context was assembled (Unix seconds), so the prompt can express ages rather than
absolute times the model has no clock for.

node.description: The node being explained — the root cause, after any roll-up hop.

recent_changes.description: Recent audited configuration changes touching this node.

root_node_id.description:
Id of the node being explained. Differs from the one the operator clicked whenever the
roll-up hop fired, and it is what a generated report is filed under — a report explains the
cause, so it belongs to the cause.

timeline.description: Cross-signal timeline for the window, oldest first.

upstream.description:
Inventory ancestors, nearest first. Present even when healthy: "the parent is fine" is
evidence that the failure is local to this node.

window_secs.description: How far back the timeline reaches.

IncidentSignal.description:
One dated signal on an incident timeline (`incident_correlate`).

`Serialize` because an RCA report stores the timeline it was grounded in alongside the answer:
the UI shows the two together so a reader can check the explanation against its evidence rather
than taking it on faith (ADR-029).

InterfaceHeatmap.description:
A links × time grid. `values[i][j]` is link `i`'s throughput at `timestamps[j]`, so every row
is the same length and the client can shade cells without bounds checks.

partial.description:
`true` when the link set covers only the groups the calling account may see and links it is
entitled to may be missing. Always `false` for an account with unrestricted visibility.

InterfaceRow.description:
One interface row for the node-detail Interfaces tab: stored metadata joined with query-time
`rate()`/`latest()` metrics. Utilization is derived here and never stored (ADR-012).

The four `*_power_*_dbm` bounds are the transceiver's **own** acceptable window, as the module
reports it — not a threshold anyone configured in Yagra, and nothing alerts on them. They exist
so a client can say whether a light level is healthy, which a bare dBm figure cannot: −7 dBm is
fine on one module and failing on another. They are `null` for every interface that is not
optical, and also for optical ones whose vendor dialect publishes no thresholds — ENTITY-SENSOR
-MIB (RFC 3433) defines none at all, so a standards-based agent reports power without a window.
A pair the module reported implausibly (low above high, or outside a transceiver's physical
range) is dropped by the poller rather than passed on, because a wrong window accuses a healthy
link. Same units as the readings: dBm, normally negative (ADR-062 Inc.4).

`if_duplex` and `if_type` describe the physical link (ADR-063 Inc.1). `if_duplex` is `half` or
`full` as the device negotiated it, and `null` whenever that is not known — which covers a device
that does not implement EtherLike-MIB, a port that is down and so has negotiated nothing, and a
device answering `unknown`. ⚠️ Expect `null` on optical ports and do not read it as a fault:
IEEE 802.3 defines no half duplex above 1 Gbit/s, so there is nothing to negotiate. The field
earns its place on copper, where a duplex mismatch is a real misconfiguration. `if_type` is the
IANAifType integer (6 = ethernetCsmacd); it is what distinguishes "duplex does not apply to this
interface" — a loopback, a tunnel, a dialer — from "we could not read it".

InterfaceSeries.description:
Per-interface time-series for the node-detail Interfaces pane: In/Out throughput in **bits per
second** and in **packets per second**, In/Out errors, and In/Out discards.

Only the throughput pair has two units, and that is a property of the MIB rather than a
shortcut: IF-MIB counts errored and discarded frames but never their octets, so
`in_errors`/`out_errors`/`in_discards`/`out_discards` are packets per second and there is no
bits-per-second form of them to ask for.

`in_ucast_pps`/`out_ucast_pps` are **unicast only** (`ifHCInUcastPkts`/`ifHCOutUcastPkts`);
multicast and broadcast frames are not counted. The name says so rather than the documentation
alone, so that a future total can be added as a new field instead of silently changing what an
existing number means. Two consequences for a client: on a link carrying heavy broadcast the
packet rate reads low, and dividing bits by packets overstates the average frame size.

Errors and discards are separate because their causes are: an error is a frame that arrived
damaged (cabling, optics, NIC), a discard is a frame the device chose to drop with nothing wrong
with it (congestion, queue overflow, ACL). Reading one for the other sends an operator to the
wrong place, so the UI draws them as two charts rather than one — ADR-046 Inc.4.

`rx_power_dbm`/`tx_power_dbm` are the transceiver's received and transmitted optical power in
**dBm**, and differ from the six above in three ways worth knowing (ADR-062). They are gauges,
not counter rates — the value is read as reported, not differentiated. They are **normally
negative**: a healthy receive level is roughly −3 to −20 dBm, and 0 dBm means one milliwatt, not
"nothing". And they are **populated only for optical ports** — a copper port, a virtual
interface, or a device whose transceiver MIB Yagra does not speak leaves both arrays entirely
`null`, which is the intended way for a client to tell an optical interface from any other.
The figure is the **module's** reading; a multi-lane transceiver (QSFP) reports its first lane
rather than an aggregate, and per-lane series are deliberately not offered.

All ten share one `timestamps` axis — the union of returned points, with `null` in the gaps —
so the chart gets aligned series rather than ten independently-indexed ones. Derived at query
time (ADR-012); empty when there is no history. The packet counters entered the default
collection set in ADR-060 and the optical readings in ADR-062, so on a deployment upgraded from
an earlier version those arrays are empty for every window predating that upgrade while the bps
arrays are populated.

InterfaceTopEntry.description: One ranked interface in a fleet interface Top-N.

if_speed_bps.description: Configured speed (bits/sec) for util%; `null` if unknown.

value.description: bits/sec for throughput metrics, errors|discards per second otherwise.

JsonExtract.description: One number to lift out of a JSON response body and record as a metric.

metric.description:
The metric name to record the value under, e.g. `queue_depth`. Must match
`[A-Za-z_:][A-Za-z0-9_:]*` and must not be one of the names the monitor already emits.

path.description:
Dot-separated path to the value, e.g. `data.queue.depth` or `items.0.value`. Array elements
are indexed by number; `items[0].value` is accepted and means the same thing.

Not a JSONPath expression: the path names exactly one location, so the rule always produces
either one number or nothing.

Language.description:
What language the answer should be written in.

The prompt is always English — instructions in one language keep the model's behaviour stable —
but the *answer* follows the reader. An operator reading a Japanese UI should not get an English
explanation of their own network.

LdapConfigInput.description: The save payload from the Settings page.

bind_password.description:
Write-only credential. Two-valued, **not** three: `None` keeps what is stored, a non-blank
value replaces it. An empty string is a validation error rather than "clear", because a bind
with a DN and no password is an unauthenticated bind that a permissive directory answers
`success` — so "no password" is not a configuration, it is a silent downgrade to anonymous.

LdapConfigResponse.description: The directory configuration, or `null` when none has been saved.

oneOf.description:
`null` rather than a 404: "not configured" is the normal state of a fresh installation, and
the settings form wants to render its empty self rather than an error.

LdapConfigView.description: The configuration as the Settings page shows it — **never** the bind password.

ca_cert.description:
The operator-supplied CA certificate, in PEM. A certificate is public, so unlike the bind
password it round-trips through the form rather than being write-only.

has_bind_password.description: True once a bind password has been stored, so the form can say "set" without revealing it.

LdapSecurity.description:
How the connection is protected. **Two variants, both TLS** — there is deliberately no plaintext
option, so `ldap://` cannot be configured into existence and the bind password cannot cross the
wire in the clear. Adding one later would be a certificate-verification-disable flag by another
name and needs the same argument (ADR-041 decision 2).

LdapTestBody.description: Which account, if any, the test should look up.

username.description:
A username to resolve. Optional: with none, the check still proves the connection, the TLS
trust and the service account's bind. With one, it also reports the DN, the groups and the
role that user would receive — **without** binding as them, so it can neither be used as a
credential-testing proxy into the directory nor push anybody towards their domain's lockout
threshold.

LdapTestResult.description:
The Test button's result.

Staged rather than a single boolean on purpose. This probe cannot prove that *logging in* works,
because it deliberately never binds as the user (see [`probe`]) — so an `ok: true` alone would
be read as "login works" when the directory may still refuse simple binds, or the account may be
disabled. Naming the stages says exactly how far it got.

note.description: What this probe did not test, so a green result is not over-read.

role.description:
The role this user would receive. **`None` means they would be denied** — the commonest
misconfiguration, and one the login form reports as an indistinguishable wrong password.

subject_present.description:
Whether the entry carried the configured id attribute — the flag, not the value. Its absence
is the failure this field exists to surface, and the value itself is of no use here.

LdapTestStage.description: One step of the Test button's report.

detail.description: Why it failed, or what it found. Truncated — this is remote-influenced text.

LinkDirection.description: Which end of a link is upstream.

LinkOverrideAction.description: What an operator has decided about a link, overriding whatever the derivation produces.

LinkOverrideList.description: Every operator decision visible to the caller.

LinkOverrideRequest.description: A decision to record about one link.

a_node.description:
One endpoint. Order is not significant — the pair is canonicalized before storing, and a
`direction` is re-expressed to match.

oneOf.description: Which endpoint is upstream. Required when `action` is `direction`, rejected otherwise.

note.description: Free-text note for whoever reads this decision later.

LinkOverrideRow.description: One operator decision about one link.

a_node.description:
The lower-ordered endpoint. Endpoints are stored in a canonical order, so this is not
necessarily the one that was submitted first.

oneOf.description: Which endpoint is upstream. Present only when `action` is `direction`.

LinkSource.description: What kind of evidence produced a link, ordered strongest first.

oneOf.description: `null` until a provider has been configured — the normal state of a fresh installation.

providers.description: Every provider the operator may choose, with its placeholders and its egress warning.

LlmConfigView.description: What `GET /api/v1/llm/config` returns. No secret, by construction.

has_api_key.description: True once a credential has been stored, so the form can show "set" without revealing it.

leaves_operator_boundary.description:
Whether this provider sends incident context outside the operator's own cloud. Computed
server-side so the warning the UI shows cannot drift from what the backend actually does.

LlmTestResult.description:
The provider-test outcome. `ok: false` is a *successful* request reporting a failed probe — the
provider configuration is the caller's, and the typed error is what tells them which part of it
is wrong, so this is not a 5xx.

LoginBody.description: Login request body. Never logged, never echoed.

role.description: The role it carries, so the UI can render the right navigation immediately.

token.description: The bearer token for subsequent requests.

MerakiCreated.description: How many organizations an onboarding batch created.

MerakiDeviceConfig.description:
A node's Meraki-device binding (1:1 with the node). No secrets: the org API key is held by the
`meraki_orgs` row's credential and inlined by core at dispatch time (ADR-018/020).

network_id.description: The Meraki networkId the device belongs to.

org_id.description: The Meraki organizationId (the API path segment) — denormalised for display.

org_uuid.description: Internal handle of the owning `meraki_orgs` row.

serial.description: The device serial — the join key returned by the org-bulk endpoints.

MerakiEnumeration.description:
What the import wizard reads in one call: the org's network scope, and the devices not yet
imported.

MerakiImported.description: How many devices an import created.

MerakiPolling.description: The global Meraki polling kill switch.

MetricDimension.description: The dimension a metric's series carry, which decides how it can be read.

MetricKind.description: What a metric's values represent over time.

MetricPoint.description: One point of a time series: Unix-seconds timestamp and value.

MetricRange.description: A time-series window for one node metric.

MetricReading.description: Latest reading for one node metric.

MetricStatus.description: Whether a metric is configured for collection, has data, or both.

MibEntry.description: One catalog entry returned by the API.

MonitoringGapRow.description:
One `monitoring_gaps` row (API shape). A gap is one core↔poller **visibility outage**: core
stopped hearing from the poller (partition or the poller went down) and later saw it again. If the
poller was alive but partitioned, its store-and-forward buffer backfills the metrics for the
window on reconnect (Phase 3); alerts are *not* backfilled (they resume from "now").

ended_at.description: End of the gap window (RFC 3339 — core heard from it again).

listeners.description:
Passive listeners the poller had bound when the gap began (e.g. `syslog:514`, `trap:162`).

Empty ⇒ the poller had none, so the gap cost no passive data. Non-empty ⇒ whatever those
listeners would have received in the window is **gone**: syslog, traps and flow exports are
