fire-and-forget, so unlike active polling there is no buffer to backfill from. (SNMP informs
are the exception — the sender retries until acknowledged.)

pool.description: Pool it serves.

started_at.description: Start of the gap window (RFC 3339 — core's last contact before the outage).

MuteScope.description: Whether a mute targets a single node or a whole folder group (recursive).

Neighbor.description:
One observed adjacency.

The first three string fields are the **identity**; everything below them is payload. Payload
changes still append a history row (a peer that was reimaged is a real change on that port), but
they never split one link into two records.

capabilities.description: What the peer says it is, normalized across both protocols.

local_ifindex.description:
The local `ifIndex`, when the protocol genuinely supplies one. CDP indexes its cache by
`ifIndex` so this is exact; LLDP's `lldpLocPortNum` is an arbitrary local index that only
*often* equals `ifIndex`, so LLDP records leave this `None` rather than guess.

local_port.description:
The local port, as the device names it: LLDP renders `lldpLocPortId` by its subtype, CDP
uses `cdpInterfaceName`. Falls back to `port <n>` / `ifindex <n>` when the naming table has
no row, so the record still has an identity rather than being dropped.

remote_chassis.description: The peer's chassis id, rendered by subtype: LLDP `lldpRemChassisId`, CDP `cdpCacheDeviceId`.

remote_mgmt_addr.description:
The peer's management address, from `cdpCacheAddress` for CDP and from `lldpRemManAddrTable`
for LLDP. `None` when the peer advertised none.

remote_platform.description: `cdpCachePlatform` — the peer's hardware/software platform string (CDP only).

remote_port.description: The peer's port id, rendered by subtype: LLDP `lldpRemPortId`, CDP `cdpCacheDevicePort`.

remote_port_desc.description: `lldpRemPortDesc` — the peer's own description of its port.

remote_sys_name.description: `lldpRemSysName`. CDP has no separate system name (its device id serves both).

NeighborCapability.description:
What the peer says it is, as one vocabulary shared by both protocols.

LLDP reports this as a `BITS` value over `lldpRemSysCapEnabled` and CDP as a four-byte mask over
`cdpCacheCapabilities`; the two bit layouts have nothing in common. Normalizing them here is
what lets the UI render one column — the alternative is a per-protocol legend, which is the
"same fact in two shapes" the extensibility rules exist to prevent.

neighbors.description: The adjacency as of this change.

prev_neighbor_key.description: The content key this replaced; `null` marks the first observation ever recorded for the node.

NeighborConfig.description: How this deployment discovers connectivity: CDP/LLDP neighbours and interface addresses.

arp_enabled.description:
Whether ARP / IPv6-neighbour walks are issued at all. Omitted on update leaves it unchanged.

Off unless an operator turns it on: this walk reads a table sized by the network rather than
by the device, and it is the only discovery walk here that costs a busy switch measurable
work. What it buys is the only answer nothing else can give — which hosts are on your
segments that Yagra is not monitoring.

arp_interval_secs.description:
How often each SNMP node's ARP / IPv6-neighbour tables are walked, in seconds. Omitted on
update leaves it unchanged.

enabled.description: Whether CDP/LLDP neighbour walks are issued at all.

interval_secs.description: How often each SNMP node's neighbour tables are walked, in seconds.

l3_enabled.description: Whether interface-address walks are issued at all. Omitted on update leaves it unchanged.

l3_interval_secs.description:
How often each SNMP node's interface-address tables are walked, in seconds. Omitted on
update leaves it unchanged.

max_interval_secs.description: Largest cadence this deployment accepts, in seconds.

media_enabled.description:
Whether media-type collection is issued at all. Omitted on update leaves it unchanged.

On unless an operator turns it off. It reads `ifMauTable` — one row per Ethernet port on the
device itself, once an hour — which is what fills the Interfaces tab's Media column.
⚠️ Many devices do not implement MAU-MIB at all; on those the walk costs one query and
returns nothing, and the column stays empty. Turning this off changes nothing for them.

media_interval_secs.description:
How often each SNMP node's media type is collected, in seconds. Omitted on update leaves it
unchanged.

min_interval_secs.description: Smallest cadence this deployment accepts, in seconds.

routing_enabled.description:
Whether routing-adjacency collection is issued at all. Omitted on update leaves it unchanged.

On unless an operator turns it off. This is what finds the links that share no subnet — a
point-to-point `/32`, an unnumbered OSPF link, an eBGP session across a segment — which the
shared-subnet rule structurally cannot see. The tables it reads are sized by the device's own
peering mesh, and the routing table itself is never walked: it is probed one destination at a
time.

routing_interval_secs.description:
How often each SNMP node's routing adjacency is collected, in seconds. Omitted on update
leaves it unchanged.

NeighborHistory.description: One page of adjacency changes, newest first.

oneOf.description: Pass back as `before_at`+`before_id` for the next page; `null` ⇒ this was the last one.

NeighborHistoryCursor.description: Keyset cursor for the next page (ADR-019 — never OFFSET).

NeighborProto.description:
Which discovery protocol reported an adjacency.

Kept on every record rather than normalized away: a switch running both protocols reports the
same physical link twice with *different* identities (LLDP names the peer by chassis MAC, CDP by
hostname), so collapsing them would mean guessing that two differently-identified rows are one
link. Showing both, labelled, is the honest answer.

NeighborSet.description:
Every neighbour a node reports on one observation, as a set.

The unit of storage is the whole set per node, not one row per adjacency, because a partial walk
must never read as "every neighbour disappeared". The poller reports the set it could observe,
core replaces it atomically, and a failed walk sends no set at all — so nothing is written. A
per-adjacency table would need an explicit "this is complete" flag to get the same guarantee.

truncated.description:
Whether [`MAX_NEIGHBORS_PER_NODE`] was hit and rows were dropped. Reported rather than
silently swallowed — a truncated view that looks complete is worse than no view.

NodeAssignment.description:
`GET /api/v1/nodes/:id/assignment` — the node's effective pool, where that pool came from, and
which poller currently holds it.

pool.description: Effective pool: the node's own, else the nearest ancestor folder's, else the default.

pool_source_group_id.description: The folder that supplied the pool, when `pool_source` is `group`.

NodeBindings.description:
Set/clear a node's profile + bound credential and its descriptive maker/model, and optionally
move it to a different poll-pool. The node-edit UI loads the current values and resends them, so
an unchanged field is preserved.

pool.description:
Poll-pool assignment (ADR-009). **Absent** = leave the pool unchanged; `""` (or whitespace)
= clear it to the `default` pool; otherwise move the node to that pool (validated as a
NATS-subject-safe token). See [`validate_pool_update`].

oneOf.description: Default: the node's own overrides, each with its id and scope.
`?resolved=true`: the effective set after profile defaults, as the poller sees it.

NodeCollection.description:
The two shapes `GET /nodes/:id/collection` answers with, as one type.

`#[serde(untagged)]`, so the bytes are the same bare array either arm always sent — the union
exists because the response shape depends on a *query parameter*, which OpenAPI cannot express,
and an undescribed body pushed the difference onto the client to guess. The stored view carries
item ids and scope; the resolved view is the poller's effective set and has neither.

NodeDetail.description:
One node's configuration detail, including its bindings (profile/credential/parent) so the
node-detail page can show and edit them. Live mode only (PostgreSQL inventory).

oneOf.description: DNS-monitor config when this node carries a `dns_checks` row; `null` otherwise.

group_id.description: The group this node belongs to; `null` ⇒ ungrouped.

kind.description:
**What this node is** — the kind the scheduler actually polls it as, resolved by the one
precedence in [`NodeKind::resolve`].

The three configs below are the raw rows, and a node is not guaranteed to carry only one:
the API edge refuses a second, but rows predating that guard exist. Reading the configs and
concluding a kind from whichever is non-null is how the node page came to show a URL-monitor
health card for a node the poller was treating as a Meraki device. Branch on this instead.

oneOf.description: Cisco Meraki binding when this node carries a `meraki_devices` row; `null` otherwise.

pool.description:
The node's **own** poll-pool (ADR-009/020); `null` ⇒ it inherits from its folder, else the
default pool. Deliberately the raw stored value, not the effective one, so the edit form can
tell an explicit assignment from an inherited one — the *effective* pool (and which poller
currently holds the node) comes from `GET /nodes/:id/assignment`.

oneOf.description: URL-monitor config when this node carries a `url_checks` row; `null` otherwise.

vendor.description: Descriptive maker/model, editable from the node detail.

NodeFacts.description: The subset of a node the model may see. Notably not the credential binding.

pool.description: Poller pool — usually the site, which is often the diagnosis ("everything in branch-osaka").

tags.description: Operator-set grouping attributes, capped and sorted for a deterministic prompt.

NodeGroupAssignment.description: Move a node into a group (or `null` to ungroup). Used by the inventory tree (drag/move).

NodeGroupRow.description: A folder in the inventory tree.

NodeId.description:
Stable identifier for a monitored node.

A UUID, not a name or address — both of which can change over a node's life.

NodeKind.description:
A node's monitoring kind: the thing that decides which poll jobs it produces.

Variants are declared in **precedence order**, which is the order [`NodeKind::resolve`] applies.
A node should carry at most one single-purpose row — the API edge refuses the second — but a row
can predate that guard, so resolution has to be deterministic rather than depend on which lookup
happened to run first.

Before this type the same question was answered in three places that could disagree: the
scheduler's Meraki short-circuit, the scheduler's URL-beats-DNS resolution, and the node-detail
API — which applied no precedence at all and handed the UI every config it found, so a node the
scheduler polled as Meraki could render a URL-monitor health card next to it.

NodeMetricEntry.description: One metric on one node: what it is, whether it has data, and how it must be read.

metric_kind.description:
Gauge vs raw counter. A counter's stored value is an odometer reading, so chart it with
`rate=true` rather than plotting it directly.

series_count.description: How many series share this name on this node — the fan-out behind one entry.

NodeNameEntry.description: One resolved node id → display name (unresolved ids are omitted; the caller keeps the raw id).

NodeNamesReq.description: Request body for `POST /api/v1/node-names`: the node ids whose display names to resolve.

NodePage.description: One keyset page of the inventory.

next_cursor.description:
Pass back as `cursor` for the next page; `null` ⇒ this was the last one. Always `null` in
filter mode, which returns a single capped page by design.

truncated.description:
Filter mode only: matches exist that this answer does not contain, because the page hit its
cap or the candidate scan hit its ceiling. Always `false` while paging.

A separate field rather than something the client infers from `nodes.len()`, because once
the server rejects candidates after the query those two stop meaning the same thing: a
filter that scans 5,000 rows and keeps 3 returns three rows and is still incomplete.

NodeParentAssignment.description:
Set (or clear) a node's **dependency parent** (upstream). `parent_id: null` removes the
dependency. This is the alert-suppression edge (parent down ⇒ suppress children, ADR-015) —
distinct from `PUT /nodes/:id/group`, which moves the node in the inventory folder tree.

NodePlacement.description:
Drag-reorder a node within (or into) a group, positioning it relative to a sibling node.
`group_id` is the destination group (`null` ⇒ ungrouped); `before`/`after` name the sibling to
land next to (both omitted ⇒ append to the end). At most one of before/after may be set.

NodeRow.description: A monitored node. `credential_id` is a reference only — see the module docs.

NodeSearchResult.description:
One node-picker result: id + display name + address. Deliberately excludes credentials and
bindings — the picker only needs to show and select a node.

NodeState.description: The current state of a monitored node or check.

NodeStatus.description:
One node's live status: its display state plus the alerts currently attributed to it, so node
detail can show *why* it is down without re-deriving from the list.

group_id.description: The group this node belongs to (for the inventory tree); `null` ⇒ ungrouped.

kind.description:
**What this node is**, and therefore how it is polled — the value that distinguishes a URL
or DNS monitor from an ordinary ICMP/SNMP device in the inventory.

Resolved by `NodeKind::resolve`, the same function `GET /nodes/{id}` and the scheduler ask,
so a list row can never disagree with the detail page it opens.

pool.description:
The node's **own** poll-pool; `null` ⇒ inherited from its folder, else the default pool.
The tree's pool picker edits exactly this value, so it is what marks the active choice —
the *effective* pool (and the poller holding the node) comes from `/nodes/:id/assignment`.

sort_order.description: Manual order within the group (the tree sorts members by this, then by name).

NodeSuppressionOptOut.description: Whether this node is excluded from derived alert suppression.

opt_out.description: `true` ⇒ this node's alerts always stand on their own, whatever the derived graph says.

NoteCode.description:
Something the export or the import did that the operator would not otherwise see.

A silent drop is the failure mode that matters here: a bundle that quietly left out half the
rules imports without error and the operator finds out during an incident.

NotifyEvent.description:
Which point in an alert's life produced this notification.

Templates branch on it — a resolve usually wants different wording from a fire — so it is a
variable rather than three separate template fields.

OfferBlock.description: Why a release cannot be installed.

OfferDirection.description: Which way a release would move this deployment.

OidcCallbackBody.description: OIDC callback body: the `code` + `state` the WebUI forwards from the IdP redirect.

OidcProviderInput.description:
Create/update payload from the admin UI. `client_secret` is write-only: `None` on update keeps
the stored value (so editing other fields doesn't require re-entering the secret).

kind.description: Which IdP product this is. Omitted ⇒ `generic`.

OidcProviderKind.description:
Which IdP product a provider was configured for.

Descriptive only: the login handshake is driven by `issuer`, `scopes` and `groups_claim`, and
behaves identically whichever product is named here. `generic` means the provider was defined
field by field rather than from a product's shape.

OidcProviderSummary.description: Provider metadata for the admin API — **never** includes the client_secret.

has_secret.description: True once a client_secret has been stored (so the UI can show "set" without revealing it).

kind.description: Which IdP product this provider was configured for.

OidcSession.description:
A session minted by a completed SSO login — the same shape local login returns, deliberately, so
the WebUI stores a token the same way whichever path produced it.

Ok_.description: `{"ok": true}` — the body of a successful mutation that has nothing else to say.

Permission.description: A discrete capability checked at the API edge.

PermissionInfo.description: One permission in the role/privilege matrix.

dispatched.description:
How many poll jobs went to the bus. Results arrive asynchronously on the normal result
path, so this confirms dispatch, not completion.

pool.description:
The pool the jobs were published to — the node's *effective* pool, which may be inherited
from its folder rather than set on the node.

PolledBy.description: Which poller currently polls a node — the node detail's "Polled by" fact.

poller_id.description: The owning poller; set only in the `assigned` state.

PollerAnchorRequest.description: Where a poller attaches to the monitored network.

node_id.description:
The node the poller sits behind. `null` clears the anchor, returning the poller to being
placed by its own reported addresses.

PollerInfo.description:
One poller in the `GET /api/v1/pollers` response — a merge of the live registry (current
status/telemetry) and the durable inventory (so an offline poller still lists). No secrets.

anchor_node_id.description:
The node this poller attaches to, naming where it sits in the derived dependency graph.
`null` ⇒ core places it from `mgmt_addrs` instead.

caps.description:
Optional capabilities this poller's build advertises (`raw-capture`, `flow-relay`,
`http-auth`, `http-body`, `self-upgrade`). Empty when the poller is offline, and empty from
an N-1 build — **absence means "cannot", never "unknown"**, which is the same reading core
applies when it decides whether to send a poller work that depends on one.

cpu_pct.description:
Current host CPU utilization % (0–100) from its latest heartbeat; `null` when the poller is
offline or on an N-1 build without host telemetry.

first_seen.description: First durably-recorded contact (RFC 3339); `null` if not yet persisted.

has_token.description:
Whether this poller has a bus token of its own (ADR-065). `false` means it is admitted by
the deployment-wide bootstrap secret, which every poller was before tokens existed and which
a co-located poller on an unencrypted internal bus still is.

last_seen.description:
Last durably-recorded contact (RFC 3339); `null` for a live poller not yet persisted (it
registers within the 60s inventory-upsert throttle window).

listeners.description:
Passive-event listeners it has bound (e.g. `syslog:514`, `trap:162`). Empty when offline.

Worth reading before restarting a poller: unlike active polling, nothing can take these over
and nothing backfills them, so whatever they would have received while it was down is gone
(the same set `monitoring_gaps` stamps onto a healed gap).

mgmt_addrs.description:
Interface addresses the poller reported for itself. Empty for an older poller build, and
empty for a containerized poller whose only address is a container-network one.

pool.description: Pool it serves (live view wins; else the durable row).

results_total.description: Poll results core has consumed from it since core started.

status.description: `"online"` when it is beating within the offline window, else `"offline"`.

token_issued_at.description: When its token was issued, RFC 3339. `null` when it has none.

version.description: Build version from its latest heartbeat (or the durable row when it is offline).

working_set_nodes.description: Working-set node count it last reported (0 when offline / never reported).

working_set_specs.description: Working-set spec count it last reported.

PollerLag.description: A poller a single press of Upgrade would leave on its current build.

version.description: What it is running now; `null` when it has never reported a version.

PollerNodeRef.description: One node in the poller drill-down.

pool.description: The pool it serves; `null` unless it is live.

state.description:
`assigned` (live, working set known), `offline` (unknown or not beating), or `unknown`
(this core is an HA standby and runs no coordinator).

total.description: Nodes in its working set, before the page cap.

truncated.description: Whether `nodes` is a capped page of `total`.

PollerTokenRequest.description: What a new site needs, beyond its own name.

host.description:
The hostname or IP address the site will dial. Must be one the bus certificate covers, or
the site's connection fails with nothing visible centrally. Defaults to the first name on
the certificate that is not an internal one.

pool.description:
The pool this poller serves. Only used when the poller is not in the inventory yet — an
existing poller keeps the pool it reported.

port.description: The bus port at that address. Defaults to 4222.

PollerUpgradePlan.description:
Who an upgrade carries along, and who it leaves behind.

`null` on the response rather than an empty plan when the updater has not said which pollers
share its compose project: "no poller is left behind" and "nobody asked" are different answers,
and only one of them is safe to render as a reassuring zero (the lesson ADR-045 paid for).

manual.description: Pollers that stay on their current build until someone upgrades them by hand.

with_core.description:
Pollers this operation replaces: the ones in core's own compose project, plus any that
advertise `CAP_SELF_UPGRADE`.

PollersResponse.description: The `GET /api/v1/pollers` body: the fleet of pollers + the per-pool summary.

PoolAssignment.description:
Move a node (or a folder) to a poll-pool, or clear it back to inherited. Absent or `""` ⇒ NULL
(inherit from the folder, else the default pool).

PoolOption.description: One pool offered by the pool picker.

live.description:
Whether a live poller currently serves it. A pool with none takes the legacy per-job path
onto a subject nothing subscribes to, so its jobs are silently discarded — the picker has to
say so rather than present it as an equivalent choice.

PoolOptions.description: The pools that exist, for the assignment picker.

PoolSource.description:
Where a node's effective pool came from, so the UI can say "inherited from the Tokyo folder"
rather than just showing a name.

PoolSummary.description:
One pool in the `GET /api/v1/pollers` response — node count vs. live pollers, its dispatch mode,
and a warning when it has nodes but no live poller (they would go unmonitored).

mode.description: `"working_set"` when a live poller serves it, else `"legacy"` (per-job fallback).

nodes.description: Non-Meraki nodes assigned to this pool.

pool.description: Pool name (`default` for unassigned nodes).

warning.description: `"nodes_without_live_poller"` when the pool has nodes but no live poller, else `null`.

PreferencesSaved.description: A save's acknowledgement. The document is not echoed back — the client already has it.

PreviewProblem.description: One field that could not be used.

message.description: The engine's message, including the offending line where it knows it.

PreviewRequest.description: A template to render against a representative alert.

event.description: Which point in an alert's life to render: `fire`, `resolve`, or `suppress`.

kind.description: The channel kind the template is for. Decides whether the body has to be valid JSON.

PreviewResult.description: What the template produces, or what stopped it.

body.description: The rendered body, under the same rule.

json_valid.description:
Whether the rendered body parses as JSON. `null` when this channel kind sends the body as
plain text, where the question does not apply.

problems.description: One entry per field that could not be rendered and fell back. Empty on success.

subject.description:
The rendered subject. Yagra's built-in wording when the subject is not overridden, or when
rendering it failed — which is exactly what would be sent.

ProfileBody.description: Create/update body. `category` is optional on create (defaults to generic SNMP).

poll_interval_secs.description:
Per-profile polling-interval override, in seconds. Omitted/`null` ⇒ inherit the global
default; when present it must fall within `[MIN, MAX]`.

ProfileId.description:
Stable identifier for a device profile / device-class (e.g. "Cisco router").

Profiles carry the polling templates and default thresholds a node inherits.

ProfileSummary.description: A device-class/profile row for the API (id + name + role/vendor metadata).

category.description: Functional role token (kebab-case `ProfileCategory`) — the UI's grouping key.

poll_interval_secs.description: Per-profile polling-interval override (seconds); `None` ⇒ inherit the global default.

vendor.description: Vendor label, if known (descriptive metadata only — never a TSDB label).

ProviderChoice.description:
What the Settings form needs to render one provider choice.

Served from the backend rather than hardcoded in the WebUI so the egress warning cannot drift
from what the code actually does: [`ProviderKind::leaves_operator_boundary`] is the single
definition, and the checkbox that warns about it reads the same value the adapter obeys.

credential_optional.description: Whether the credential may be omitted (Vertex on GKE/GCE uses Workload Identity instead).

leaves_operator_boundary.description:
True when picking this sends hostnames, addresses, topology and syslog outside the
operator's own cloud.

needs_project.description: Whether this provider needs a GCP project + region (Vertex) rather than just an API key.

entries.description: The ranked rows, highest first, at most the requested `limit`.

partial.description:
`true` when this ranking covers only the groups the calling account may see and entries it
is entitled to may be missing. Always `false` for an account with unrestricted visibility.

items.description: One ranked interface in a fleet interface Top-N.

if_speed_bps.description: Configured speed (bits/sec) for util%; `null` if unknown.

value.description: bits/sec for throughput metrics, errors|discards per second otherwise.

entries.description: The ranked rows, highest first, at most the requested `limit`.

partial.description:
`true` when this ranking covers only the groups the calling account may see and entries it
is entitled to may be missing. Always `false` for an account with unrestricted visibility.

items.description: One ranked node in a Top-N result.

name.description:
Display name, joined from PostgreSQL (ADR-011); falls back to the id string if the node has
since been deleted.

entries.description: The ranked rows, highest first, at most the requested `limit`.

partial.description:
`true` when this ranking covers only the groups the calling account may see and entries it
is entitled to may be missing. Always `false` for an account with unrestricted visibility.

RcaAnswer.description:
The parsed explanation. **Every field is plain text and must be rendered as text, never as HTML
or markdown** — this is model output, and the model was itself reading untrusted device output.

confidence.description: How sure the model says it is.

dependents.description: Whether the other affected nodes are consequences of it.

raw.description:
Set when the reply was not parseable JSON: the model's text, verbatim and bounded. Its
presence is what tells the UI to render one prose block rather than empty sections.

root_cause.description: What most likely failed, and why the evidence says so.

summary.description: One sentence an on-call engineer can act on.

force.description: Regenerate instead of serving a cached report. Still rate-limited.

language.description:
UI language tag (`ja`, `en-GB`, …). The instructions stay English; the answer follows the
reader. Unknown tags fall back to English rather than failing.

node.description:
The alerting node. May be a symptom of an upstream failure — the context builder follows
`root_cause` to the incident before assembling anything.

window_secs.description: Timeline window in seconds; clamped by the orchestrator. Defaults to an hour.

RcaConfidence.description: How sure the model says it is. `unknown` means it answered outside this set, or not at all.

RcaReport.description:
A stored report. `body` carries the answer and its evidence; `summary` is lifted out of it so a
list view does not have to fetch the whole thing.

body.description: The answer and the evidence it was grounded in.

cached.description:
Whether this response came from the cache rather than a fresh call. Not a column — it
describes *this* delivery of the report, not the report.

ReleaseOffer.description:
A release the operator could move to, with the direction and the verdict already decided by the
server — the comparison is semver, and it is the same rule that decides whether a rollback is
safe.

oneOf.description: Why it must not be offered, or `null` when it can be.

core_digest.description: Resolved image digest, when the sidecar could resolve one.

direction.description: Whether this moves forward or back.

ReportBody.description:
A report's contents: the answer, the evidence it was grounded in, and the language it was
requested in.

evidence.description: Everything the model was told, exactly as it saw it.

language.description: Which language the answer was requested in.

transcript.description:
What the model looked up for itself, in order (ADR-028 WS-G). Empty on a single-shot run,
and on every report written before agentic retrieval existed.

ReportDefinition.description: A report definition (reusable template), as served to the API.

ReportDefinitionBody.description: Create/update body for a report definition.

ReportRun.description: A run row for the saved-reports list (without the heavy `result_*` payloads).

ReportRunDetail.description: A run plus its rendered result (the viewer / export endpoints).

ReportSchedule.description: A schedule row (joined with its definition's name for display).

ReportScheduleBody.description: Create/update body for a schedule (preset cadence).

ReportScheduleStatus.description: Outcome of a schedule's most recent firing.

RetentionPolicy.description: The full retention policy: the editable windows plus every row of the table.

rows.description: Every retained subject, including the ones no API can change.

settings.description: The windows this endpoint can change.

RetentionRow.description: One line of the retention table.

enforcement.description: How the window is applied: `pg_prune`, `store_ttl`, `store_flag` or `unlimited`.

field.description: Which field of `settings` this row binds to, or `store_owned` / `unlimited`.

note.description: Operator-facing explanation. For a read-only row it names the flag that does change it.

store_configured.description:
Whether the backing store is configured in this deployment. A row for an unconfigured
optional store retains nothing.

store_reported.description:
What the store itself reports for a `store_flag` row, verbatim (e.g. `12`, `30d`). Absent
when the store is unreachable or is running its own default — in which case the value is
genuinely unknown and is not guessed.

subject.description: Stable identifier for the retained data, e.g. `alert_history`.

tunable.description:
Where it can be changed: `settings` (here), `store_flag_read_only` (the store's own
command-line flag), or `by_decision` (not retained on a schedule at all).

unit.description: Unit of `value`: `days`, `hours`, or empty when the row has no configurable number.

value.description: The configured window, for rows this deployment controls.

alert_linked_days.description: Days to keep alert history, node-state snapshots, DNS chain changes and matched events.

diagnostic_days.description:
Days to keep on-demand diagnostics: Troubleshoot analysis runs with their findings, and
generated AI root-cause reports. Optional — omitting it sets the default (90).

flow_days.description: Days to keep traffic-flow records, applied as a ClickHouse table TTL.

report_run_days.description: Days to keep generated report runs.

unmatched_event_hours.description: Hours to keep passive events that matched no rule.

Role.description: Predefined roles, ordered least → most privileged.

RoleInfo.description: One role in the matrix: its metadata and the permission keys it grants.

builtin.description: Built-in roles are fixed (custom roles are not configurable yet).

permissions.description: The keys of the permissions this role grants.

RotatedToken.description: A freshly rotated ingest token — the second and last place the plaintext appears.

RoutingRule.description: A routing rule: enabled alerts of `severity` (None = any) fan out to `channel_ids`.

RuleTestResult.description:
The tester's answer. A compile failure is reported **in-band** rather than as a 400: the whole
point of the tester is to show the operator what is wrong with the pattern they are typing, and
a 400 would be rendered as a request failure instead of inline next to the field.

id.description: Correlation id for this run; it appears on the status the updater writes.

maintenance_window_id.description:
The fleet-wide maintenance window opened for the duration, or `null` if one could not be
opened (the run still proceeds — silencing is a courtesy, not a precondition).

RunStatus.description:
The most recent run the sidecar performed (`status.json`).

Survives core restarting mid-operation, which is the whole reason it is a file: the process that
asked for the upgrade is not the process that sees it finish (ADR-050 decision 3).

command.description:
`apply` or `bundle` — the commands that produce a run. (`refresh` writes no status: it
changes nothing, and a status file of its own would blank the last upgrade's outcome.)

finished_at.description: Unix seconds when it ended; `null` while it is still running.

id.description: The run id core generated when it wrote the request.

message.description: Human-readable detail, especially the reason for a failure or refusal.

started_at.description: Unix seconds when the run began.

target.description: The release the run targets, when it targets one.

core_version.description: The crate version this core was compiled from.

hostname.description: The container's hostname, which is how a replica identifies itself in the logs.

source_ref.description: The commit the image was built from (`/etc/yagra-source-ref`); `null` outside a container.

SavedFinding.description: One finding as the cross-run search returns it: the finding, plus the run it came from.

at.description:
When the finding was written (RFC 3339). Pass it back as `before`, with `id` as
`before_id`, to fetch the next page.

job_id.description: The analysis run that produced this finding.

node_id.description: The node this finding is about; absent for a fleet-level finding.

tool.description: Which diagnostic produced it, as that run recorded it (e.g. `anomaly`).

ScanStatus.description: A scan's current status returned by the API.

done.description:
Terminal or not. Kept alongside `state` because it is part of the published contract (the
MCP `get_config(kind="discovery_scan")` tool serves this type straight through), and derived
from `state` rather than stored, so the two cannot disagree.

pool.description: The pool the job was **actually published to**; `null` for the global subject.

probed.description:
Targets probed so far, and the sweep's total. An address counts once a probe has been
addressed to it, which is not the same as the sweep having finished identifying it.

scanning.description: The address the sweep is currently at (the next unprobed target), while running.

started_at.description:
When the sweep was accepted (RFC 3339) — RFC 3339 rather than epoch millis to match the
discovered-endpoint rows this API already serves.

updated_at.description: When a result last moved this scan forward (RFC 3339).

ScanSummary.description:
One row of the scan list — everything [`ScanStatus`] has except the candidates themselves.

The omission is the point: 20 retained scans of up to 1024 candidates each would make listing
them far more expensive than the question deserves. A caller that wants a scan's candidates asks
for that scan.

candidate_count.description: How many devices answered so far.

pool.description: The pool the job was **actually published to**; `null` for the global subject.

SchedulerStatsSnapshot.description: A point-in-time view of [`SchedulerStats`] for the API.

assignment_mirror_writes_total.description:
Redis assignment-mirror rewrites issued since start (S18). Flat across steady-state sweeps —
an unchanged working set skips the rewrite — so growth tracks real assignment churn.

deltas_published_total.description: Working-set deltas core has published to pollers since start (ADR-020).

jobs_last_round.description: Jobs published in the most recent round (legacy per-job dispatch only).

last_sweep_unix_ms.description: When the last poll round was dispatched (Unix ms), or `None` if none yet.

pools_legacy.description: Pools served in legacy per-job mode in the most recent sweep (no live poller).

pools_working_set.description: Pools served in working-set mode in the most recent sweep (a live poller owns them).

results_total.description: Total poll results consumed since start.

snapshots_published_total.description: Working-set snapshots core has published to pollers since start (ADR-020).

SchemaState.description: What this database's migration history says about itself.

applied_count.description: How many migrations have been applied.

oneOf.description: The binding compatibility floor, or `null` when every applied migration is reversible.

latest_version.description: The newest applied migration version; `null` only on a database with none.

oneOf.description: Unrestricted visibility.
Visibility limited to these group identifiers.

Groups.description: Visibility limited to these group identifiers.

Scope.description:
Which slice of the inventory an account may see: everything, or a named set of node groups.

A node is visible if it belongs to an allowed group or to anything beneath one. A node in **no**
group is visible only under `All` — an unassigned node is not leaked to a scoped account.

ScopeLevel.description:
The scope a threshold is defined at, ordered least → most specific: `Node` wins over `Group`,
which wins over `Profile`, which wins over `Global` (every node).

SecretsMode.description: How secrets appear in a bundle. See the module docs for why there is only one variant.

SectionDef.description: A report-section type the user can add to a report.

SectionSetting.description: A configurable setting on a section (rendered generically by the builder).

SetPassword.description: Reset-password request body. The password is hashed before storage and never logged.

SetProfileTemplates.description: Replace-all body for a profile's attached templates.

SettingOption.description: One selectable choice for a `select` setting.

Severity.description:
How serious an alert is. Variants are declared low → high so the derived
`Ord` ranks `Critical` above `Warning` above `Info`.

ShadowAlert.description: One node whose suppression would change if the deployment moved to the derived graph.

node_id.description: The node whose active alert is affected.

root_cause.description: The node the derived graph blames, when it has one.

ShadowEdge.description: One node whose parent set differs between the two graphs.

SourceKind.description:
Which received stream a destination tees. Kept here (rather than in core) so the DB `CHECK`
strings, the API validation and the WebUI all agree on one spelling.

StaleNode.description: A node returning no fresh data (silent failure / blind spot).

StartScan.description:
Start-scan body: explicit target IPs (the WebUI expands a CIDR), candidate stored credentials by
id, and ad-hoc communities.

pool.description: Poll-pool to run the sweep in (ADR-009/020). Absent/empty = legacy global discovery.

snmp_when_unreachable.description:
Try SNMP on addresses that do not answer ICMP.

Absent means **no**. Earlier releases had no such option and tried every address in the
range with every candidate credential, which is why sweeping a /24 took minutes; set this to
get that behaviour back, and with it a device that filters ICMP but answers SNMP.

StartedScan.description: The accepted scan's id, for polling its status.

StoredCollectionItem.description: A stored collection item with its id and scope, for the API (the scheduler ignores id).

StoredEventRule.description: A stored event rule (API shape; the engine compiles enabled ones).

StoredExemption.description: A node released from an inherited suppression, until the suppression it was carved out of ends.

until_at.description: RFC 3339. Server-computed from the coverage in force when the release was made.

StoredMute.description:
A stored mute (API shape). A `node` mute silences one node (optionally one check via
`metric_name`); a `group` mute silences every node under a folder group (recursive). Exactly
one of `node_id` / `group_id` is set, per `scope_kind`.

StoredThreshold.description: A stored threshold rule with its scope and id (id is for the API; the engine ignores it).

StoredWindow.description: A stored maintenance window (API shape; times are RFC 3339 text at the edge).

active.description: Whether the window covers "now" (computed at read time for the UI).

SubjectKind.description:
Which kind of thing an alert is about: a monitored `node`, or a poller `pool` when Yagra is
reporting on its own polling coverage.

SystemHealth.description: Yagra's own health: the reachability of its backing services.

bus.description: NATS — **inferred** from a recent scheduler sweep, not a direct ping.

flow.description: ClickHouse (flow store, ADR-031) — likewise reachable when not configured.

logs.description:
VictoriaLogs (event log, ADR-024) — reported reachable when not configured (events then live
in PostgreSQL), so an unconfigured log store never degrades `overall`.

overall.description: `"ok"` when every dependency is reachable, else `"degraded"`.

search_semantics.description:
How a plain event-search term matches here: whole words on a log-store deployment,
any substring on PostgreSQL. Reported rather than assumed — see `EventSearchSemantics`,
which explains both why the two differ and why a client checks for this field's presence.

web_tls.description:
The WebUI's TLS certificate. Reported unhealthy only when someone has to act: it has expired,
or an imported certificate is inside its last 30 days. A self-signed one renews itself.

SystemHostsResponse.description: Core plus every poller that reports host telemetry.

TableResult.description: What the import did to one table.

TemplateBody.description:
A channel's notification-template override. Both fields are replaced together; `null` or blank
on a field restores Yagra's built-in wording for it.

TemplateItem.description: One metric in a template, with its id, for the template editor.

TemplateSummary.description: A collection template row for the API (id + name + description + metric count).

TemplateVariable.description: One name a notification template may reference.

always_present.description:
Whether every alert carries it. A variable that is not always present is *undefined* when
absent: it renders as empty text, and `{{ name | default("…") }}` supplies a fallback.

TestResult.description:
The outcome of a one-shot delivery test.

`delivered: false` is a *successful* request reporting a failed probe, not a 5xx: the
destination's configuration is the caller's, and the transport error is what tells them which
part of it is wrong. The error text is the transport's, never a payload — syslog bodies carry
credentials.

ThresholdBody.description:
A threshold rule as the caller states it — the body of both `POST` and `PUT`.

One type for both, the shape `ProfileBody` already uses. Two would be two validators, and this
repo has paid for that: URL-check and DNS-check CRUD were two copies of one writer, so the "a
node is exactly one kind" rule shipped enforced on only one of them.

ThresholdPage.description:
A capped page of threshold rules.

`total` is the count of rules **matching the filter**, not `items.len()`, so the UI can say *how
many* it is not showing. `truncated` is derived rather than left to the client comparing the
two — a client that forgets the comparison shows a complete-looking list.

total.description: Rules matching the filter, ignoring the cap.

truncated.description: Whether `items` is a prefix of the matching rules rather than all of them.

ThresholdRule.description: A threshold rule for a single metric.

critical.description: Value at/over which the node is `Critical`. `None` = no critical level.

dwell_samples.description:
Hysteresis: consecutive samples the breach must hold before transitioning,
to damp oscillation at the threshold. `0`/`1` = transition immediately.

metric.description: Stable metric name this rule applies to (e.g. `cpu_util`).

warning.description: Value at/over which the node is `Warning`. `None` = no warning level.

ThroughputRange.description:
Fleet aggregate ingress and egress, aligned onto one shared timestamp axis.

Both arrays are the same length as `timestamps`, with `null` where that side has no sample.
The chart draws two series against one x-axis, so aligning here rather than client-side is what
keeps a missing ingress point from silently shifting egress by one slot.

TlsCertSource.description: Where a certificate came from, and therefore whether core may replace it on its own.

TokenSurface.description:
Which authentication surface a credential may be presented at.

A personal access token authenticated `/mcp` and nothing else, so there was never a choice to
express. Now that the REST API accepts one too the two surfaces differ enough that "may
authenticate here" has to be recorded per token: `/mcp` is a curated, mostly-read tool surface,
while REST is the entire configuration API. A token minted for an AI client must not become a
configuration credential because the server learned a new trick — so the surfaces are named on
the token, and anything that does not name [`TokenSurface::Rest`] cannot reach `/api/v1`.

ToolTurn.description:
One tool the model asked for, and what it was told.

Stored for the same reason `evidence` is: an explanation whose reader cannot check what it was
based on is an assertion. Agentic retrieval makes that worse, not better — the evidence is no
longer a fixed set somebody chose, so without this nobody can tell whether the model looked at
the right thing.

result.description: What the tool answered, as the model saw it.

tool.description: The tool name, from the agent's allow-list.

TopEntry.description: One ranked node in a Top-N result.

name.description:
Display name, joined from PostgreSQL (ADR-011); falls back to the id string if the node has
since been deleted.

TopologyLink.description: One undirected link in the derived connectivity graph.

a_if_name.description: Port name on the `a` side, when a source reported one.

a_ifindex.description: `ifIndex` on the `a` side, when a source reported one.

a_node.description: One endpoint. `null` is reserved for an endpoint that is not a monitored node.

b_if_name.description: Port name on the `b` side, when a source reported one.

b_ifindex.description: `ifIndex` on the `b` side, when a source reported one.

b_node.description: The other endpoint. `null` is reserved for an endpoint that is not a monitored node.

first_seen.description: When this link was first derived (RFC 3339).

forced_parent.description:
The endpoint an operator declared upstream, when one was declared. `null` means the direction
is worked out from how far each end is from a poller.

id.description: Stable id, and the keyset cursor.

source.description: The strongest of `sources` — what to label the link with.

sources.description: Every kind of evidence that produced this link.

subnet.description: The subnet behind a shared-subnet link, e.g. `192.168.1.0/24`.

TopologyLinkPage.description: One keyset page of the derived connectivity graph, with what the last derivation run saw.

derived_at.description: When the graph was last derived (RFC 3339), or `null` before the first run.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page; `null` ⇒ this was the last one.

summary.description: Counters for everything the last derivation declined to turn into a link.

total_links.description: How many links the whole graph holds, not just this page.

TopologyLinkSummary.description: What the last derivation run observed but did not turn into a link.

ambiguous_mgmt_addrs.description:
Adjacency rows whose management address matched more than one node, so no link could be
attributed without guessing which.

bgp_links.description: Links produced from a BGP peering session.

bgp_peers_not_adjacent.description:
BGP peers that matched a monitored node but sit on no network the reporting node terminates,
so the session is not evidence of a link between them. The normal reading is iBGP between
loopbacks; a number that stays at zero on a network running iBGP means the reporting node's
interface addresses have not been observed.

cdp_links.description: Links produced from a CDP adjacency.

duplicate_addresses.description:
Addresses claimed by two or more nodes — a shared virtual IP, or a duplicate-address
misconfiguration.

l3_links.description: Links whose strongest evidence is shared-subnet membership.

lldp_links.description: Links produced from an LLDP adjacency.

ospf_links.description: Links produced from an OSPF neighbour relationship.

oversized_segments.description:
Segments with more than two members where no member could be identified as routing for the
others, so no link was drawn.

route_links.description: Links produced from a connected host route — the point-to-point links that share no subnet.

subnet_prefix_mismatch.description: Addresses sharing network bits but disagreeing on prefix length.

truncated_nodes.description: Nodes whose observation hit a per-node cap, so what is recorded for them is incomplete.

unmatched_cdp_rows.description: CDP rows whose management address matched no monitored node.

unmatched_lldp_rows.description: LLDP rows whose management address matched no monitored node.

unmatched_routing_peers.description: Routing adjacencies whose peer address matched no monitored node.

TopologyMode.description: Which dependency graph the alert engine uses.

TopologyModeRequest.description: The topology mode to move the deployment to.

TopologyNode.description: One node in the dependency/topology graph.

parent_id.description: Upstream parent in the dependency graph (`null` ⇒ a root).

root_cause.description:
Upstream node currently identified as the root cause of this node's alert (dependency
suppression), if any — lets a client collapse downstream alerts under the cause.

TopologyPage.description: One keyset page of the dependency graph.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page; `null` ⇒ this was the last one.

TopologyShadow.description: What the derived dependency graph would do, against what the manual one does.

anchors.description: Nodes the derived graph treats as roots, because a poller sits on their segment.

covered_nodes.description:
How many nodes the derived graph gives at least one upstream.

Read with `total_nodes`: a low ratio means most of the fleet would keep alerting exactly as
it does now, which is usually the point rather than a problem.

mode_since.description: When the mode was last changed (RFC 3339), or `null` if it never has been.

only_in_derived.description: Parent edges only the derived graph has.

only_in_manual.description: Parent edges only the hand-authored graph has.

opted_out.description:
Nodes an operator has excluded from derived suppression entirely.

A list rather than a count: the screen that shows the comparison is also where the exclusion
is toggled, and a count cannot tell a row whether it is the excluded one. Bounded by what an
operator typed in, not by the fleet.

unresolved_pollers.description: Poller ids that could not be placed, so an operator knows which to give an anchor.

unresolved_pools.description:
Pools with at least one poller whose location could not be resolved.

**Non-empty blocks `derived`.** A pool with no anchor contributes no roots, so none of its
nodes would ever be suppressed while every screen showed the feature as on.

would_suppress.description:
Active alerts the derived graph **would suppress** and the manual one does not.

The number to review before enabling `derived`: each of these is an alert that would stop
being raised.

would_unsuppress.description:
Active alerts the manual graph suppresses and the derived one would not — the noise
direction.

UndecryptableCredential.description:
A credential the current KEK cannot open. Carries identity only — never a length, a `key_id`,
or anything derived from the ciphertext.

UpdateCredential.description:
Update body. `name` is required; `secret` is optional — see the module doc for why omitting it
is a rename and supplying it requires `kind`.

UpdaterInfo.description: Whether the privileged updater container is deployed, and whether it is alive.

allow_bundle.description:
Whether it will install an uploaded image archive. Off unless the host's compose file turns
it on — it is the only path that can bring an image this deployment never named onto the
host, so it is gated separately from the mechanism as a whole (ADR-050 Increment 3).

bundle_max_bytes.description:
The largest archive core will accept, in bytes. Present whenever `allow_bundle` is, so the
UI can refuse an oversized file before spending an hour uploading it.

check_interval_secs.description: How often it re-checks the registry, in seconds.

fresh.description: Whether its last report is recent enough for it to be considered alive.

installed.description:
Whether this deployment has an upgrade mechanism at all — that is, whether the host wired
the hand-off directory in. `false` describes how the deployment was installed rather than
anything that went wrong: upgrading from the WebUI needs a container composition that
carries the privileged updater alongside core, so a native installation, or a composition
that does not ship it, cannot offer it. The command-line upgrade path is unaffected.

last_seen.description: Unix seconds of its last report.

paused.description:
Whether the sidecar has seen the switch turned off. Distinct from `upgrade_enabled`, which
is what this deployment *stored*: while the two disagree the change has not reached the
sidecar yet, which takes at most one of its beats.

present.description:
Whether the updater has ever reported. Meaningful only where `installed` is true, and there
it means the container is missing or has not finished starting — a fault, not a property of
the deployment.

repo.description:
The image repository it is pinned to. Fixed by the host environment and not settable over
this API.

UpgradeStatusResponse.description: The state of the upgrade mechanism and of this deployment's schema.

oneOf.description:
Releases the updater last saw in the registry; `null` when it has never looked. Carries the
raw list and why it may be empty — `offers` is the part a page should render.

enabled.description:
Whether an upgrade can be requested from here — the updater is deployed, alive, **and** the
operator's switch is on. When `false`, this response describes only what is installed.

oneOf.description: The most recent run, finished or in flight; `null` when none has ever been requested.

offers.description:
The moves this deployment could make, each with its direction and whether it is allowed.
Excludes the running version. Empty when the updater has found nothing.

oneOf.description:
Which pollers this operation would replace and which it would leave on their current build
(ADR-051). `null` when the updater has not reported the pollers in its own compose project —
core cannot tell a co-located poller from a remote one on its own, and an invented answer
would read as fact.

schema.description: Applied migrations and the compatibility floor they imply.

upgrade_enabled.description:
The operator's switch, as stored by this deployment. Separate from `enabled`, which also
depends on the updater being alive: this one says what was *chosen*, and it is what the
toggle in Settings ▸ Upgrade reflects.

enabled.description: Whether upgrading from the WebUI is permitted on this deployment.

UrlCheckConfig.description:
A node's URL-monitoring configuration (1:1 with the node). No secrets: the optional auth
`credential` is a reference; core resolves/inlines the decrypted value (ADR-018/020).

oneOf.description: Optional keyword rule applied to the response body.

body_max_bytes.description:
How many bytes of the response body to read (default 65536, range 1024–1048576). Applies to
both `body_match` and `json_extract`; the body is not read at all unless one of them is set.

oneOf.description:
Optional auth credential (Basic/Bearer/custom header). A reference only — core resolves it
to an [`HttpAuth`] and inlines that into the poll job, the same path SNMP credentials take.

expected_status.description: Which status codes count as healthy (default: any 2xx).

json_extract.description:
Values to lift out of a JSON response body and record as operator-named metrics.

Each rule adds one gauge per poll. A rule whose path is missing, or whose value is not a
number, records **nothing** for that poll rather than a zero.

verify_tls.description:
Verify the TLS certificate chain (default `true`). Turning it off is an explicit operator
choice — it is never disabled silently.

UrlCheckRow.description: A URL / HTTP endpoint monitor's configuration (1:1 with its node).

body_match.description: The monitor's response-body keyword rule, if it has one.

body_max_bytes.description: How many bytes of the response body the monitor reads.

json_extract.description: The monitor's JSON extraction rules, if it has any.

UserKind.description:
How an account authenticates, which decides whether it can log in interactively at all.

`Service` is the reason this enum exists. An API token needs an owner so that disabling or
deleting the owner takes the token with it — but binding an unattended integration to a *person*
means it dies when they change teams. A service account is a machine identity: no password, no
IdP subject, and therefore no way to sign in. It exists to own tokens.

UserSummary.description: User-account metadata for the API — never includes the password hash.

auth_source.description:
How the account authenticates: `"local"` (password), `"oidc"` (external identity provider),
`"ldap"` (directory bind), or `"service"` (a machine account that cannot sign in).

created_at.description: Account creation time (RFC 3339 text; no chrono types cross the API edge).

enabled.description:
Account status: a disabled account is retained for the audit trail but cannot
authenticate (defaults to `true` for accounts created before this column existed).

last_login_at.description:
Most recent successful login (RFC 3339 text), or `None` if the account has never
logged in.

scope.description:
Which slice of the inventory this account may see: `"All"`, or the node groups it is
limited to. An Admin account is always `"All"` — administration is fleet-wide.

WebTlsImport.description: A certificate chain and its private key, in PEM.

certificate.description:
The full certificate chain in PEM, leaf first. A private key in this field is rejected —
send it in `private_key`.

private_key.description:
The matching private key in PEM: PKCS#8, PKCS#1 or SEC1, and not passphrase-protected.
Never returned by any endpoint.

WebTlsRegenerate.description: Which names a regenerated self-signed certificate should cover.

names.description:
Hostnames and IP addresses to put in the subject alternative name. If empty, the deployment's
defaults are used — loopback plus the server's own hostname, which is rarely the address
browsers actually use.

WebTlsResponse.description: The WebUI's TLS certificate, plus one fact about how this deployment is exposed.

api_port_is_public.description:
Whether Yagra's API port is reachable beyond the server itself. When `true`, the API is also
available over plain HTTP on that port, so the encrypted WebUI is not the only way in.

oneOf.description: The certificate being served, or `null` if none has been established yet.

WebTlsView.description: The certificate the WebUI is serving. Never includes the private key.

certificate.description:
The certificate chain in PEM, leaf first. Safe to distribute — this is what a client would
add to a trust store or pass to `curl --cacert`.

expires_in_days.description: Days until expiry; negative once it has passed.

fingerprint_sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the certificate, matching what a browser displays.

imported_at.description: When this certificate was imported or generated, RFC 3339.

imported_by.description: The account that imported it, if it was imported by a signed-in user.

issuer.description: Distinguished name of the issuer. Equal to `subject` for a self-signed certificate.

key_algorithm.description: Key type and size, for example `RSA-2048` or `ECDSA P-256`.

key_unreadable.description:
Whether the private key can still be decrypted. `false` means the encryption key has changed
or been lost: the certificate cannot be served or renewed until it is imported again.

materialized.description:
Whether the web server is currently serving this certificate. `false` means it is stored but
has not reached the web container yet.

not_after.description: End of the validity window, RFC 3339.

not_before.description: Start of the validity window, RFC 3339.

sans.description: The hostnames and IP addresses this certificate is valid for.

subject.description: Distinguished name of the certificate's subject.

WindowScope.description:
How a maintenance window is scoped. The first three mirror threshold scoping (ADR-013):
`Node` = node id, `Profile` = device-class id, `Group` = a tag value. `FolderGroup` is the
hierarchical inventory group (resolved recursively, incl. subgroups, ADR-022) — the scope the
All Nodes right-click uses. It is *not* a threshold concept, so it stays local to maintenance
rather than extending the shared [`yagra_common::ScopeLevel`].

bearer.description: Either a session token from `POST /api/v1/auth/login` (short-lived; what the WebUI uses), or a personal access token (`yat_…`, Settings ▸ API tokens) whose surfaces include `rest`. A token issued for `mcp` only is refused here with 401. An API token acts as the account that owns it, so its role **and** its visibility scope are capped at that account's current ones, and it stops working when the account is disabled or deleted; it cannot administer users, and endpoints that identify the signed-in account (`/auth/me`, the personal dashboard) answer 403 to it.
